# MutinyBIM

> Open-source, browser-based building information modeling (BIM) engine for every trade, built for many people and AI agents editing one model at once. Agents work by writing scripts with the kit (@permitzip/bim-script), checking and previewing them, and applying them after a person approves.

The tool server lists at most 10 core tools by default (168 in all, opt-in by family). Write a script rather than looking for a tool. Start from an example script, check it, preview it, apply it.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules for coding agents working in this repository
- [Connect an agent](docs/CONNECT-AN-AGENT.md): connecting Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others to the tool server
- [Scripting](docs/SCRIPTING.md): how scripts work: kinds, reads, parameters, checks, preview and approval
- [Example scripts](docs/reference/examples.md): whole scripts to copy
- [Recipes](docs/reference/recipes.md): worked tasks

## Reference

- [ctx: the script context](docs/reference/script-kit/ctx.md): What a script's `run(ctx)` gets: reading the model slice it declared, sending edits, running calcs and reads, proposals, labels and reports.
- [units](docs/reference/script-kit/units.md): Typed lengths and other measures. Every length a kit function takes is a `units.*` value, never a bare number.
- [building](docs/reference/script-kit/building.md): Levels, grids, walls, doors, windows, floors, ceilings, roofs, stairs, rooms and spaces.
- [routes](docs/reference/script-kit/routes.md): Duct, pipe and conduit runs: sizes, systems, slopes, where a run starts and ends, and connecting into a run.
- [equipment](docs/reference/script-kit/equipment.md): Placing parts (equipment, fixtures, devices) by type, and their connectors.
- [parts](docs/reference/script-kit/parts.md): Making part types: a part's bodies, connectors and parameters.
- [PartBuilder](docs/reference/script-kit/part-builder.md): The builder `parts.part()` returns: boxes, extrusions, sweeps, connectors and parameters on one part type.
- [documents](docs/reference/script-kit/documents.md): Views, sheets, schedules, tags, notes, dimensions and the rest of a drawing set.
- [checks](docs/reference/script-kit/checks.md): Checks a script runs on its own output before a person sees it.
- [defineScript](docs/reference/script-kit/define-script.md): The one top-level function: a script's kind, what it reads, its parameters and its `run`.
- [Edit commands](docs/reference/commands.md): every command ctx.edit takes, with its fields
- [Calcs](docs/reference/calcs.md): every calculation ctx.calc runs
- [Pack reads](docs/reference/reads.md): every read ctx.read runs
- [Tool server tools](docs/reference/mcp-tools.md): every MCP tool, by family
- [Add-ons](docs/reference/add-ons.md): the trade add-ons and what each contributes

## Optional

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): kernel, add-ons, sync and the model server
- [Add-on contract](docs/ADD-ON-CONTRACT.md): the extension points an add-on plugs into
- [Your first add-on](docs/YOUR-FIRST-ADD-ON.md): a tutorial
- [Scripting coverage](docs/SCRIPTING-COVERAGE.md): what scripts can do of each add-on, and what is missing
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): sign-off, setup, tests and the bedrock rule

<!-- AGENTS.md -->

# Notes for coding agents

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first: sign-off, setup, tests and the
bedrock rule apply to agents exactly as to people.

**Start here:** the example scripts in `packages/bim-script/examples`
(`bim_script_reference({ example: "<name>" })` serves them). Copy the closest
one rather than starting from nothing; each runs as one
`bim_run_script` → check → `bim_apply_output`. Run one locally with
`npm run example -- <name>`. `packages/bim-mcp/__tests__/examples-run.test.ts`
runs them all; keep it green when you change the kit.

## Tools: script-first, ten at most

The script API is the product. AI writes code: an agent acts on a model by
writing a script with the kit (`packages/bim-script`), checking it, previewing
it and applying it after the person approves. The tools only run, check and
apply scripts, plus a few reads.

- The default tool list (the core pack) is at most 10 tools.
- New capabilities go into the script API and `bim_script_reference`, with a
  worked example, never as new default tools.
- Extra tool families are opt-in only: `--packs <family,…>`,
  `/packs/<family>/mcp`, or turned on in a session with `bim_enable_pack`
  (the server then sends `notifications/tools/list_changed`).
- Never make "all tools" the default anywhere: plugin bundle, hosted app, CLI.
- Never add a tool to the core pack without the maintainer's approval.
  `packages/bim-mcp/__tests__/core-tool-budget.test.ts` enforces the limit.
- What a script does of each add-on tool, and what is still missing:
  `docs/SCRIPTING-COVERAGE.md`. Close a gap in the kit, not with a tool.
- `docs/reference/` and `llms.txt` are generated from the code. After a change
  to the kit, a command, a calc, a pack read, an add-on or a tool, run
  `npm run docs` and commit the result; never edit them by hand.

### Why

Nov 7, 2026: we spent several thousand dollars building 159 add-on MCP tools
that no AI can use well. Models get confused by long tool lists. AI writes
code: the script API is the product. Stop building new MCP tools for features.
Build script API functions, documented in `bim_script_reference` with a worked
example.

### Forbidden

- A new MCP tool for a feature a script can do.
- Making "all tools" the default anywhere.
- Growing the core pack past 10 tools.

## Every screen uses the shared theme and components

MutinyBIM has one look, defined once in `packages/bim-ui`:

- **Theme**: the `--mutiny-*` CSS variables (colors, fonts, radius) from
  `mutinyDefaultTheme` and `mutinyDarkTheme`. React screens get them from
  `MutinyThemeProvider`; server-rendered pages get the same variables from
  `themeStyleSheet()`. Light, dark and the computer's setting all come from
  there.
- **Components**: `Button`, `Badge`, `Alert`, `Empty`, `Separator`,
  `Spinner`, `Tooltip`, `ToggleGroup`, `ThemeToggle`, `Card`, `Input`,
  `Textarea`, `NativeSelect`, `Label`, `Field` and the brand marks, exported
  from `@permitzip/bim-ui`.

Rules for every screen, in the editor and in every app under `apps/`:

1. Draw controls with those components. Do not hand-roll a button, input,
   card, badge or alert.
2. Take every color, font and radius from a `--mutiny-*` variable. No hex
   colors, no inline `style` colors and no one-off stylesheets that pick their
   own palette. Layout utilities (flex, grid, gap, width) are fine.
3. Check the screen in light and in dark before you finish.
4. If a screen needs a primitive bim-ui lacks, add it to
   `packages/bim-ui/src/ui/` (colors from `--mutiny-*` only) in the same
   change, then use it. Never style a local copy instead.
5. Printed sheets and issued PDFs are the exception: paper stays black on
   white and never reads the theme.

<!-- docs/CONNECT-AN-AGENT.md -->

# Connect an AI assistant

MutinyBIM is built for AI agents to work beside people. This page says how an
outside assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Cursor, Codex or any other) works
with this repository **today**, and what is coming.

The short version:

| Today | Coming |
| --- | --- |
| Connect any MCP client to the tool server (`packages/bim-mcp`) and change a model by running scripts, approving each change; add every other tool family with `--packs all`. | Hosted services for the packs that need one (Autodesk Docs linking, branches, reading pictures with AI). |
| Write and check scripts with the scripting kit and its command line. | The full editor in the open packages, so tools and screens share one host. |
| Drive a live model over the sync protocol, as the demo's scripted agents do. | A hosted free app you can point your own assistant at. |

## Rules that hold for every agent

- **An agent never has more access than its person.** An agent acts for one
  signed-in person, under its own actor id tied to that person, with exactly
  that person's capabilities.
- **Same commands, same checks.** An agent sends the same intent commands as
  the editor. The server re-runs every command on the current model and
  refuses conflicts in words. Nothing an agent sends is trusted as written.
- **People approve.** Script output is a set of ordinary edit batches with a
  label and a preview, meant to be approved by a person before it lands. How
  approval looks is up to the host application.
- **Your assistant, your bill.** MutinyBIM does not call an AI model itself.

## 1. The tool server

`packages/bim-mcp` serves MutinyBIM's agent tools over the Model Context
Protocol, on stdio (your assistant starts it) or streamable HTTP (your
assistant connects to a URL).

### The tools

The core pack is small on purpose. Its main job is running the scripts your
assistant writes; everything else a model can do (walls, routes, equipment,
circuits, sheets, schedules) is a function in the scripting kit, so the
assistant learns the kit instead of a hundred tools.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `bim_script_reference` | Start here, once per conversation. A short index: the workflow, the kit's functions by name, whether scripts can run here. Then `search` a topic, `topic` for one function or recipe whole, `command` for one command's fields, `example` for a whole script. |
| `bim_check_output` | Lint and syntax of a script with line numbers, kit functions and commands that don't exist, what its reads would send, or the kernel's checks on an output. Runs nothing. |
| `bim_run_script` | Runs a script and checks its output: a preview. Saves nothing; returns what would change, `apply_with` and the script's `script_id`. |
| `bim_apply_output` | Lands the preview as one undo step after you approve. Re-runs the script, with what the preview ran with, and lands only exactly what was previewed. |
| `bim_save_part_type` | Saves a part script's part types and the script to the library after you approve. |
| `bim_model_summary` | Counts by kind, levels, zones, systems, open issues, questions, and the revision read. |
| `bim_query_elements` | Elements by kind, class, area and discipline, with the facts an edit needs. |
| `bim_inspect_network` | One element's connected system, up to its equipment. |
| `bim_validation_issues` | Open validation issues with the elements involved. |

Add-on packs register more tools on the same server through the extension
point (`BimToolPack` in `packages/bim-mcp/src/server.ts`), without touching
the core. Pack membership lives in one place, the `packages/bim-plugin`
catalogue.

**Every other tool family** (parts and equipment, routing and fittings,
electrical and plumbing, views, sheets, drafting and detailing, drawing sets,
schedules, coordination lint, groups and phases, linked models) is in
`packages/bim-mcp-packs`. Start the server with `--packs all` to add them
(159 tools on top of the core's 9). They keep the tool names and arguments
hosted products use, so they take a `project_id` (any uuid on a local
server, which has one workspace). On your computer, printed sheets, issued
sets and saved pictures are written under `--files <dir>` (default
`./mutinybim-files`); schedules, firm parts, lint settings and route
defaults are kept in memory; and the few tools that need a hosted MutinyBIM
(Autodesk Docs linking, branches, reading a picture with AI, a project's
adopted code editions) answer in plain words that they aren't available
here. Every edit any pack makes asks you first, like the core's.

### Start it

```bash
npm install
npm run mcp:http                     # http://127.0.0.1:3333/mcp
# or
npm run mcp                          # stdio (normally your assistant starts it; see below)
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--http`, `--port <n>`, `--host <h>` | stdio | Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`. It listens on this computer only unless you pass `--host`. |
| `--model-server <ws url>` | in memory | Use a running model server, for example the demo's `ws://127.0.0.1:3095/sync` (`npm run demo`), with `--model <id>` for each model. |
| `--model <id>` | `demo` | Models to serve (in memory: each starts with one level). |
| `--approve ask\|auto` | `ask` | `ask`: every change asks you in your assistant first. `auto`: changes land without asking. A local demo only. |
| `--read-only` | off | Reads and previews only; every edit and save is refused. |
| `--no-scripts` | off | Scripts are refused. |
| `--packs none\|all` | `none` | `all` adds every add-on tool family to the core. |
| `--files <dir>` | `./mutinybim-files` | Where printed sheets, issued sets and saved pictures go. |

The in-memory model server keeps nothing after the server stops.

### Approvals

Every change asks you before it lands. The server asks through your
assistant (MCP elicitation): you see what will land and approve or decline;
the assistant cannot answer for you. If your assistant cannot ask (it does
not support elicitation), changes are refused in words and nothing lands.
`--approve auto` lands changes without asking; use it only for a local demo
on your own computer.

### Where scripts run

On your computer, each script runs in a fresh Node process with Node's
permission model (it reads only its own bundle and writes nothing), an empty
environment, and the kit's caps (1 GB memory, 30 s, 2 MB of output). Node
cannot deny a process the network, so this runner is for **your own
scripts on your own computer only**. Never use it to run other people's
scripts on a shared server: a host that does runs the same two runner files
(`packages/bim-script-runner`) on a sealed machine with a deny-all network.

### Connect your assistant

Use the absolute path to your checkout in place of `/path/to/mutinybim`.

**Claude Desktop** (`claude_desktop_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mutinybim": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/path/to/mutinybim/packages/bim-mcp/bin/mutinybim-mcp.mjs"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add mutinybim -- node /path/to/mutinybim/packages/bim-mcp/bin/mutinybim-mcp.mjs
# or, with npm run mcp:http running:
claude mcp add --transport http mutinybim http://127.0.0.1:3333/mcp
```

**Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json` in your project, or `~/.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mutinybim": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/path/to/mutinybim/packages/bim-mcp/bin/mutinybim-mcp.mjs"]
    }
  }
}
```

or, over HTTP: `{ "mcpServers": { "mutinybim": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3333/mcp" } } }`.

**ChatGPT** (a custom connector in developer mode) and other hosted
assistants connect from the internet to an HTTPS address, so they cannot
reach `127.0.0.1`. To try it, run `npm run mcp:http` and put it behind an
HTTPS tunnel you control, for as long as you are trying it, and keep
`--approve ask`. The local server has no sign-in, so anyone who has the
tunnel address can read your models; never share it.

**Any other MCP client:** stdio with the command above, or streamable HTTP at
`http://127.0.0.1:3333/mcp`.

### A worked example

Ask your assistant: *"In the MutinyBIM model `demo`, add a second level 4 m
above Level 1 with a script."* It does this:

1. `bim_script_reference` with no arguments: scripts can run here, the
   workflow, the kit.
2. It writes the script:

   ```ts
   import { defineScript } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
   export default defineScript({
     kind: "layout",
     reads: { levels: true },
     parameters: {},
     run(ctx) {
       ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: "level-2", name: "Level 2", elevationMm: 4000 });
     },
   });
   ```

3. `bim_check_output({ model_id: "demo", script: { source, reads: { levels: true } } })`:
   `status: "ok"`, no findings, and `script_id: "scr_…"`. This is the only
   time the script's text is sent.
4. `bim_run_script({ model_id: "demo", script: { id: "scr_…" } })`:
   `status: "previewed"`, `changes: { creates: 1, edits: 0, deletes: 0 }`, and
   `apply_with`. The model has not changed.
5. `bim_apply_output(apply_with.args)`: `apply_with.args` names the script by
   its id, not its text. Your assistant shows you *land "…" in model demo as
   one undo step: 1 new, 0 changed, 0 deleted. Approve?* You approve; the
   answer is `status: "saved"` with the new revision.
6. `bim_model_summary({ model_id: "demo" })` now counts two levels.

If the model moved between the preview and the approval, the apply answers
`stale_preview` and nothing lands; the assistant runs the preview again.
This exact sequence runs in CI
(`packages/bim-mcp/__tests__/oss-local-end-to-end.test.ts`).

### A script is sent once

An assistant pays for every character it sends and reads, on every step. So
the tools keep each script it sends and give it a short id:

| The assistant sends | When |
| --- | --- |
| `script: { source, reads }` | The first time. `reads` may be left out when the script declares them as plain values. |
| `script: { id }` | Any later call about the same script: the preview after a check, a second preview with other values. |
| `script: { id, replace: [{ old, new }] }` | A fix after an error. `old` is exact text that is in the script once (`all: true` changes every place). A replacement that isn't found, or is found more than once, changes nothing and says which one. The answer carries the changed script's own id. |
| `script: { key, version }` | A script saved in the library. |

What an id is tied to, so nothing can be swapped between the preview you saw
and the change you approve:

- The id is a fingerprint of the person, the script's text and its reads.
  Another text, other reads or another person is another id, and only the
  person who sent a script can use its id.
- A successful preview is recorded with what it ran with: the model, the
  level or zone, the values, the selection, and a fingerprint of its output.
  `bim_apply_output` and `bim_save_part_type` by id run exactly that again
  and land only that output. A call that names other values, another
  selection, another area or another model is refused.
- An id lasts 36 hours, longer than an approval can wait. After that the
  answer is "That preview has expired; run the script again".

Answers are kept short too: a search returns its two best matches whole and
the rest by name; a preview lists at most 40 part types and a few plan
pictures; long error messages are cut and say so. Each says how to get the
rest.

### Hosting the tool server

A product that hosts MutinyBIM gives the tool server its own answers to five
questions through one interface (`BimToolHost` in
`packages/bim-mcp/src/host.ts`), and the tools stay the same:

- **Who is calling:** the person and the agent run acting for them.
- **May they do it:** the host checks read access before a model is read and
  edit access before an edit, before any model server contact; it is asked
  before a script runs; its library says who may save.
- **Approval:** a gate decides before anything lands. A host with its own
  approval cards and a durable record of each decision passes the call
  through only after the person approved (`hostDecidedApproval`); the local
  host asks through the client (`elicitationApproval`).
- **Where scripts run:** a sealed machine per conversation, never the
  process serving the tools.
- **The model server:** sessions on the model server as that person.

One more, optional, answer saves an assistant most of what it would send
again: **where scripts are kept between calls** (`previews` on the host, a
`ScriptPreviewStore` with two methods, `put` and `get`, that stores each
record whole under its id). A hosted product keeps them somewhere that
outlives a restart and its longest approval wait (the hosted app uses its
account database); one person's computer uses `MemoryScriptPreviewStore`. The
tools check the owner, the expiry and the id themselves, so the store has no
rules of its own. A host that gives no store still works: a preview then
returns the whole script in `apply_with.args`, as before.

`registerBimCoreTools(server, host)` puts the core pack on a server a host
already runs (its own transport, sign-in and middleware);
`createBimToolServer({ host, packs })` makes a ready one.

## 2. Work in the repository


The simplest way: open this repository in an AI coding assistant and ask it to
build an add-on, write a script, fix a bug or add a test. Point it at:

- [ADD-ON-CONTRACT.md](ADD-ON-CONTRACT.md) for add-ons;
- [SCRIPTING.md](SCRIPTING.md) for scripts;
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
  for the rules (build on the kernel, typed units, performance budgets).

The kit reference is generated from the kernel's command schemas, so an
assistant can ask for exact command shapes:

```ts
import { searchReference, referenceMarkdown, commandFields } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

searchReference("route a duct");     // ranked commands and helpers
commandFields("route_run");          // fields and JSON Schema of one command
referenceMarkdown();                 // the whole reference as Markdown
```

## 3. Scripts and the command line

An assistant writes a script with `defineScript`, then runs and checks it
against a slice of a model:

```bash
mutinybim-script run   script.json --slice slice.json --out output.json
mutinybim-script check output.json --slice slice.json
```

`check` previews every batch against the slice and reports refusals, what
would re-open, quantity changes and lint, without changing anything. The
output is ordinary `batch_edits` that any MutinyBIM server accepts and
re-checks. Details: [SCRIPTING.md](SCRIPTING.md).

## 4. A live model over the sync protocol

A program can join a live model the same way the editor does. Start the demo:

```bash
npm run demo        # dev server on http://localhost:3095, sync on ws://localhost:3095/sync
```

Then connect with the sync client from `@permitzip/bim-sync`:

```ts
import WebSocket from "ws";
import { SyncClient } from "@permitzip/bim-sync";
import type { Actor } from "@permitzip/bim-kernel";

const actor: Actor = { id: "agent-1", name: "Layout agent", kind: "agent" };
const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:3095/sync");
let started = false;

const client = new SyncClient(
  { send: (data) => ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN && ws.send(data), close: () => ws.close() },
  actor,
  {
    // Fires once the server's welcome has arrived, and again on every change.
    onView: (model) => {
      if (started) return;
      started = true;
      console.log("model has", Object.keys(model.elements).length, "elements");
      client.publishPresence({ kind: "working", note: "Adding a level" });
      const result = client.submit({ type: "create_level", levelId: "lvl-9", name: "Level 9", elevationMm: 36_000 });
      if (!result.ok) console.log("refused before sending:", result.error.message);
    },
    onOutcome: (request, outcome) => {
      if (outcome.status === "committed") console.log("saved", request.command.type);
      else console.log("not saved:", outcome.error.message);
    },
  },
);
ws.on("open", () => client.opened());
ws.on("message", (data) => client.receive(data.toString()));
```

`client.view()` returns the model as this client sees it (confirmed edits
plus its own pending ones), or `null` before the welcome.
`packages/bim-devserver/scripts/agents.ts` is a complete example:
scripted agents that read, think, commit (sometimes from a stale base) and
report commits, rebases and conflicts.

Everyone in the demo editor sees the agent's presence and its edits live.

**On the model server** the flow is the same, with two differences: the
`hello` message carries a sign-in token and a model id, and the server asks
its authorizer what that person may do before it loads the model. A person
with view-only access gets a read-only connection. See
`services/bim-authority/README.md` and `packages/bim-sync/AUTHORIZATION.md`.

## 5. The plugin standard: tool packs, skills and MCP

`packages/bim-plugin` describes MutinyBIM's agent tools as an
[Agent Plugins 1.0](https://agent-plugins.org) package:

- **Tool packs.** About a dozen packs (core, drafting, ducts and pipes,
  electrical, plumbing, views and sheets, coordination, groups and phases,
  parts, calculations, schedules, model). An assistant connects the core
  plus only the packs a job needs, which keeps its tool list small. Each pack
  has a token cap for the tool text it may advertise.
- **One Agent Skill per pack** (`packages/bim-plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md`),
  telling the assistant how to use that pack's tools. The guidance in each
  is written by hand; its frontmatter and tool list are rendered from the
  catalogue (`npm run build:files` in the package), so a tool moved between
  packs moves in its skill too. A host app reads the same skills with
  `bimPluginSkills()` and adds its own notes on top; nothing host-specific
  is written here.
- **One MCP server entry per pack.** `renderMcpJson(baseUrl)` writes
  `mcp.json` for any server; each pack is served at
  `<base>/packs/<slug>/mcp`.
- **Add-ons bring tools too.** An add-on declares agent tools as data
  (`AGENT_TOOL_POINT`) and may group them in its own pack.

```ts
import { bimPackCatalogue, renderMcpJson, renderPackageFiles } from "@permitzip/bim-plugin";

bimPackCatalogue();                              // packs, their tools and caps
renderMcpJson("https://your-host.example/bim");  // mcp.json for your server
```

The tool server in this repository (section 1) serves the core pack. The
other packs in the catalogue are served today by host applications that
embed MutinyBIM; they move into this repository as tool server packs.

## Coming next

- **Hosted services for the packs that need one** (Autodesk Docs linking,
  branches, reading pictures with AI) in the hosted free app.
- **A sealed script runner you can run yourself:** the same runner files in a
  container with a deny-all network, for hosting other people's scripts.
- **A hosted free app** where you bring your own assistant.

Follow progress in [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md).

<!-- docs/SCRIPTING.md -->

# Scripting

The scripting kit (`packages/bim-script`, `@permitzip/bim-script`) lets a
person or an AI assistant write a small TypeScript program that makes model
edits or part types. Scripts are how agents do repetitive or parametric work:
"a receptacle every 12 ft on Level 2", "a plenum in these five sizes",
"three more floors at 13 ft".

A script never edits a model directly. It produces **ordinary edits**
(`batch_edits` of kernel commands) or **ordinary part types**. The model
server re-parses and re-runs them like any other edit, and a person approves
them. Scripts never run inside a model server.

## A first script

```ts
import { defineScript, units } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {
    count: { type: "number", label: "Floors to add", integer: true, default: 3, min: 1, max: 50 },
    height: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "ft", label: "Floor to floor", default: units.ft(13), min: units.ft(8), max: units.ft(30) },
  },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const levels = ctx.model.levels();
    let top = 0;
    for (const l of levels) if (l.kind === "level" && l.elevationMm > top) top = l.elevationMm;
    const step = units.in_(v.height, "mm");
    for (let i = 1; i <= v.count; i++) {
      ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("lvl"), name: `Level ${levels.length + i}`, elevationMm: top + i * step });
    }
    ctx.label(`${v.count} floors at ${units.in_(v.height, "ft")} ft`);
  },
});
```

What happens:

- `defineScript` checks the manifest (kind, parameters, presets, reads) and
  returns a definition any host can draw a form from.
- `v.height` arrives as a `Measure` with a unit kind, never a bare number.
  `units.ft(13)`, `units.in(18)`, `units.mm(…)`, `units.m(…)` build measures;
  `units.of(kind, value, unit)` builds any kind; `units.in_(m, "mm")` reads one
  back in a unit.
- Each `ctx.edit(command)` is parsed with the kernel's own command schema and
  applied to a working copy at once, so later reads see it. A refused step
  stops the run with the step number and the kernel's reason.
- `ctx.id(prefix)` gives ids that are the same on every run with the same
  script, values and model revision. `ctx.random()` is seeded the same way.
- `ctx.label(text)` is the one-line summary a person sees when approving.
- `ctx.calc(request)` runs an engineering calculation, `ctx.read(id, input)`
  an add-on's computed read (a panel's loads per phase, a rebalance or
  room-template plan, a duct size, a catalogue; `ctx.reads()` lists them), and
  `ctx.propose(id, request)` an add-on's proposer (receptacles by code
  spacing), each on the model as the script has it so far. A read's plan is
  sent with `ctx.editSteps(plan.command)`; proposed devices are placed with
  `ctx.acceptGhosts`.
- The kit's planners do what the editor's commands do, on the same working
  copy: `documents.autoTag`, `autoDimension`, `packSheet`, `oneLine`,
  `scheduleRows`, `checks.clashes`, `building.surfacesAt`. `bim_script_reference`
  has a worked example for each.

## Script kinds

| Kind | Makes | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | Edits | `ctx.edit` |
| `route` | Edits (runs) | `ctx.edit`, the `routes` helpers |
| `part` | Part types | `ctx.parts.define(typeId, definition)`, the `parts` builder |

A part script may not edit; an edit script may not define parts.

## Parameters

Parameter types: `quantity` (a unit kind and display unit; stored in SI),
`number` (optional `integer`), `choice`, `boolean`, `text`, and `part_type`
(a part type the model has). Each takes a label, an optional description, a
default, and bounds where they apply.

**Presets** are named sets of values (`{ id: "p24x12", title: "24 x 12 with a
10 in outlet", values: { … } }`). Values are resolved preset over defaults,
given values over both. An unknown name, a missing required value or one out
of range is refused in words.

## Reads: what a script may see

A script declares what it reads. The host sends only that **slice** of the
model, and reading past it is a plain error that names what to add.

| `reads` field | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `levels: true` | Levels and the model settings (`ctx.model.levels()`). |
| `kinds: [...]` | Every element of these kinds (`ctx.model.ofKind(kind)`). |
| `ids: [...]` or `"selection"` | These elements, or the person's selection (`ctx.model.selection()`). |
| `partTypes: [...]` | Part types matching these patterns, `*` as a wildcard (`ctx.model.partTypes()`). |
| `fields`, `rows`, `calc`, `footprint` | Field values, schedule rows, calculations and level outlines (newer reads; see the kit reference). |

`ctx.model.get(id)` returns an element or errors; `ctx.model.find(id)`
returns it or `undefined`. Elements the script's own edits made are always
readable.

## Helpers

- **`parts`**: a builder for part types. Profiles (`rect`, `circle`,
  `polygon`), bodies (box, extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, imported meshes) with
  join and cut, parameters a body can follow, connectors on faces, and symbols
  per view.
- **`routes`**: run sizes (`rect`, `round`, `oval`, `pipe`), ends
  (`atConnector`, `atRunEnd`), `routes.along(ctx, spec)` for a run through
  points (the kernel places the fittings), and `routes.branch(...)` off a
  trunk.
- **`building`**, **`equipment`**, **`documents`**: walls and openings,
  spaces, placed parts, sheets and plan views.

`searchReference(query)` and `referenceMarkdown()` give the kit reference.
It is generated from the kernel's own command schemas and the add-ons in
force, so it stays correct as the kernel changes. `starterScriptItems()`
returns five worked examples to copy.

## What a script may not do

The kit checks the source before anything runs (`checkScriptSource`,
`lintScript`). A script imports only `@permitzip/bim-script`. It may not:

- load code at run time (`import()`, `require`, `eval`, `Function`);
- use the network (`fetch`, `WebSocket`, …) or the host process (`process`);
- reach the global object;
- read the clock (`Date`, `performance`) or use timers;
- use `Math.random` (use `ctx.random()`).

These rules make a run deterministic: the same script, values and slice give
the same output.

## Output

A run returns one of:

```ts
{ kind: "edits", label, steps, batches }   // batch_edits of at most 500 steps each
{ kind: "part_types", types }              // [{ typeId, definition }]
```

Steps never include a server-only command or a nested batch.
`parseScriptOutput` re-checks an output the way a server does.

## Checks

`checkScriptOutput(model, output, options)` checks an output without
committing anything, the same way on a laptop, in CI or on a server:

- each batch through the kernel's preview, in order: refused or not, what it
  would re-open, which quantities change, and a fingerprint so an approval can
  tell when the model has moved on;
- optional lint on what each batch touched;
- for part types, the kernel's part checks, a connector report and a picture
  of each view.

Before anything runs, the kit also reads a script's source (nothing is
executed) and names the line of each mistake that would only fail in a run:

- `lintScript(source)`: what a script may not do, and its shape (one
  `export default defineScript(...)`, a kind);
- `readsWarnings(source, reads)`: a call that needs model data the reads
  don't send;
- `kitUseWarnings(source)`: a kit function that doesn't exist
  (`building.rooms` when the kit has `building.room`) and a
  `ctx.edit({ type: "..." })` whose command doesn't exist, each with the
  closest real names.

The tool server's `bim_check_output` returns all three. A check costs an
assistant far less than a failed preview.

## The command line

The kit's command line has three commands:

```text
mutinybim-script run   <script.json> --slice <slice.json> [--values '<json>'] [--preset <id>] [--out <output.json>]
mutinybim-script check <output.json> --slice <slice.json>
mutinybim-script pack  <dir> [--out <file.tgz>]
```

- **`run`** runs a library script item against a slice and writes the output.
- **`check`** checks an output against a slice and prints the report. It exits
  0 when the output is clean, 1 when not.
- **`pack`** builds an unsigned library package from a folder with a
  `mutinybim.json` manifest. A person signs it to publish.

`<script.json>` is a library `script` item: key, name, version, language,
kit range, manifest, source, license and authors
(`@permitzip/bim-library`). `<slice.json>` is a model slice
(`format: "mutinybim-slice"`), made with `sliceModel(model, reads, selection,
features)` from a model you hold, for example one received from the dev
server.

The command logic is `runCli(argv, io)` in `@permitzip/bim-script/cli`. The
kit never opens files or the network itself; the Node wrapper supplies file
access and the TypeScript loader.

## Where scripts run: the runner contract

The kit defines the contract; each environment supplies a runner
(`ScriptRunner`: `id`, `limits`, `run(request)`). Every runner must provide:

- a fresh process for each run;
- no network;
- no file access beyond the kit and the run's input;
- no child processes;
- caps no larger than `RUNNER_CONTRACT`: 1024 MB memory, 30 s wall clock,
  2 MB output.

A run that hits a cap says which one (`cap_memory`, `cap_time`,
`cap_output`) and is not retried unchanged. `script_error` means the script
threw; `runner_error` means the runner failed. `runFailureWords` turns any
failure into plain words.

Two mistakes in a script used to look like a runner failure, and now say
what they are (`script_error`, with the script's line when there is one):

- an async call the script didn't `await` that then threw: "… (thrown by an
  async call the script didn't await: put await in front of it)";
- `run()` waiting on something that never finishes: "The script ended
  without a result: run() is waiting on something that never finishes".

A `runner_error` that remains is the machine's (it didn't start, or it was
stopped from outside, most often for memory), and its words say so: run the
same script once more, don't rewrite it. A script error longer than 3,500
characters is cut, and says how much, instead of being refused whole.

`runRunnerConformance(runner, targets)` proves a runner meets the contract:
limits, fresh process, determinism, no network, no files, no child processes,
and each cap. `packages/bim-script-runner` is the runner:
`LocalScriptRunner` runs each script in a fresh Node process with
Node's permission model, an empty environment and the caps, on your own
computer (the tool server uses it; Node cannot deny a process the network,
so it is for your own scripts only), and the same two bundled files run on a
sealed machine with a deny-all network for a host that runs other people's
scripts. The kit's `runScript` still runs a script in the current process,
for tests.

## Provenance

Part types made by a script carry where they came from: the script, its
version and content hash, and the values used (`partTypeItemsFromRun`).
`regenerate` re-runs a saved script and says whether each part type still
matches.

## Scripts in other languages

`scriptJsonSchemas()` returns JSON Schemas for the manifest and the output, so
a builder in another language can produce output that `checkScriptOutput`
accepts.

# ctx: the script context

What a script's `run(ctx)` gets: reading the model slice it declared, sending edits, running calcs and reads, proposals, labels and reports.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`ctx.model`](#ctxmodel): The model as far as the script's reads go: get(id), levels, elements of a kind, the selection.
- [`ctx.id`](#ctxid): A new id, the same on every run with the same script, values and model revision.
- [`ctx.random`](#ctxrandom): Seeded randomness in [0, 1): use it, never Math.random, so every run gives the same result.
- [`ctx.edit`](#ctxedit): One kernel command, applied at once to the script's working copy (later steps see it).
- [`ctx.label`](#ctxlabel): What the edits do, in words, for the Approve card ("Receptacles every 12 ft, Level 2").
- [`ctx.report`](#ctxreport): Shows a value the script read or worked out to the agent: it comes back as `report` in bim_run_script's answer, beside the preview.
- [`ctx.parts.define`](#ctxpartsdefine): Part scripts only (kind: "part"): one part type (one size of the part) saved under its type id.
- [`ctx.calcs`](#ctxcalcs): The engineering calculations a script can run: code calcs (NEC, plumbing, fuel gas), duct friction and system pressure, pipe system reports, service size, beams.
- [`ctx.calc`](#ctxcalc): Runs one calculation on the model as the script has it so far, and returns its values (each with key, value, unit and citations) or the reason it can't.
- [`ctx.editSteps`](#ctxeditsteps): Sends a plan's edit as an add-on read or proposer returned it (one edit, or a batch such as a room template's circuits or a rebalance's moves), step by step.
- [`ctx.reads`](#ctxreads): The computed reads the model's add-ons offer, by id: panel loads (electrical.loads), the electrical check, rebalance and room-template plans, a feeder size, the electrical and plumbing catalogues, duct size advice (mechanical.duct_size).
- [`ctx.read`](#ctxread): Runs one add-on read on the model as the script has it so far and returns its answer (plain data; type it with read<T>).
- [`ctx.proposers`](#ctxproposers): The proposers the model's add-ons offer: devices placed by a code's spacing or coverage (electrical.receptacles, plumbing.cleanouts…), each with what it places on.
- [`ctx.propose`](#ctxpropose): Runs a proposer on rooms: ghost placements, each with the requirement it meets and the code clause, and a summary that says whether the rooms pass.
- [`ctx.acceptGhosts`](#ctxacceptghosts): Places the ghosts kept (all, or a filtered list) as one edit on their level, each type pinned from the starter library when the model lacks it.

## ctx.model

The model as far as the script's reads go: get(id), levels, elements of a kind, the selection. Edits the script made are visible to later reads.

```ts
readonly model: SliceReader
```

Topics: read, model, levels, selection, find

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const levels = ctx.model.levels();
    const top = levels[levels.length - 1];
    if (!top) throw new Error("The model has no levels.");
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: Number(top.elevationMm) + 4000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.id

A new id, the same on every run with the same script, values and model revision.

```ts
id(prefix?: string): string
```

Topics: id, deterministic, name

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Mezzanine", elevationMm: 2500 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.random

Seeded randomness in [0, 1): use it, never Math.random, so every run gives the same result.

```ts
random(): number
```

Topics: random, deterministic

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const jitter = Math.round(ctx.random() * 100);
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Test", elevationMm: 3000 + jitter });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.edit

One kernel command, applied at once to the script's working copy (later steps see it). Every command a person or the agent can send is accepted; bim_script_reference({ command }) shows a command's fields.

```ts
edit(command: EditCommand): void
```

Topics: edit, command, change the model, any command

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: "L9", name: "Level 9", elevationMm: 32000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.label

What the edits do, in words, for the Approve card ("Receptacles every 12 ft, Level 2").

```ts
label(text: string): void
```

Topics: label, approve card, describe

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.label("Roof level at 30 ft");
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9144 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.report

Shows a value the script read or worked out to the agent: it comes back as `report` in bim_run_script's answer, beside the preview. Plain data only (numbers, text, lists, objects); at most 50 reports and 16 KB a run. A script that only reports and makes no edits still runs (nothing to apply), and a run that stops says what it reported so far. Use it instead of throwing an error to see a value.

```ts
report(label: string, value: unknown): void
```

Topics: report, see values, debug, print, inspect, what is in the model, level ids, return data

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const levels = ctx.model.levels().map((l) => ({ id: l.id, name: l.name, elevationMm: l.elevationMm }));
    ctx.report("Levels (use the id as a level argument)", levels);
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.parts.define

Part scripts only (kind: "part"): one part type (one size of the part) saved under its type id. A layout or route script never defines part types: it lists the ids of the types it uses in reads.partTypes ("acme.rtu.*" patterns work) and places them with equipment.place.

```ts
parts: { define(typeId: string, definition: PartTypeDefinition): void }
```

Topics: part, custom part, family, part type, equipment type

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.calcs

The engineering calculations a script can run: code calcs (NEC, plumbing, fuel gas), duct friction and system pressure, pipe system reports, service size, beams. Each has an id, a title and whether it reads the model.

```ts
calcs(): readonly { id: string; title: string; domain: string; summary: string; readsModel: boolean }[]
```

Topics: calculation, calcs, list calculations, engineering calc, code calc

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const duct = ctx.calcs().find((c) => c.id === "mech.duct_friction");
    if (!duct) throw new Error("No duct friction calc here.");
    ctx.label(duct.title);
    building.level(ctx, { name: "Roof", elevation: units.ft(30) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.calc

Runs one calculation on the model as the script has it so far, and returns its values (each with key, value, unit and citations) or the reason it can't. Use the answer to decide edits: a pipe size, a slope, a breaker. Name the code edition (necEdition, plumbingEdition, fuelGasEdition); the host's adopted codes are not read from a script.

```ts
calc(request: { calc: string; inputs: unknown; necEdition?: "2020" | "2023"; plumbingEdition?: string; fuelGasEdition?: string; editions?: Record<string, string>; jurisdiction?: string; state?: string }): { ok: true; run: CalcRun } | { ok: false; reason: string }
```

Topics: calculation, size a drain, pipe size, duct size, voltage drop, service size, pressure, calc

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const drain = ctx.calc({ calc: "plumbing.size_drain", inputs: { role: "building_drain", dfu: 88, slope_in_per_ft: 0.125, serves_water_closet: true }, plumbingEdition: "2021" });
    if (!drain.ok) throw new Error(drain.reason);
    const size = Number(drain.run.values.find((v) => v.key === "size_in")?.value);
    ctx.label(`Building drain, ${size} in at 1/8 in per ft`);
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "pipe", size: routes.pipe(units.in(size), "pvc"), system: { id: "san-1", kind: "sanitary" }, height: units.ft(1), slope: { rise: units.in(0.125), per: units.ft(1) }, flow: "with_points", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(5) }, { x: units.ft(40), y: units.ft(5) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.editSteps

Sends a plan's edit as an add-on read or proposer returned it (one edit, or a batch such as a room template's circuits or a rebalance's moves), step by step. One approval still covers them.

```ts
editSteps(command: unknown): void
```

Topics: apply a plan, send the plan, batch, rebalance, room template

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: units.ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }], thickness: units.in(4), height: units.ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: "builtin:panelboard-125-208-1ph@1", at: { x: units.ft(1), y: units.ft(13) }, mark: "LP-1" });
    const proposal = ctx.propose("electrical.receptacles", { typeId: "builtin:duplex-receptacle@1", roomIds: [bedroom, living], options: { mode: "dwelling", edition: "2023" } });
    ctx.acceptGhosts(proposal.ghosts, proposal.summary);
    ctx.edit({ type: "save_catalog_entry", entry: { type: "circuit_template", name: "Dwelling unit", description: "Bedroom and living room receptacles", rules: [{ room: "bedroom", devices: "receptacles" }, { room: "living", devices: "receptacles" }] } });
    const circuits = ctx.read<{ command: unknown; message: string }>("electrical.circuit_template_plan", { template: "Dwelling unit", units: [{ panel: "LP-1", rooms: ["101", "102"] }] });
    ctx.editSteps(circuits.command);
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.reads

The computed reads the model's add-ons offer, by id: panel loads (electrical.loads), the electrical check, rebalance and room-template plans, a feeder size, the electrical and plumbing catalogues, duct size advice (mechanical.duct_size).

```ts
reads(): readonly { id: string; label: string }[]
```

Topics: what can I read, reads, add-on reads, catalogue, panel loads

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const ids = ctx.reads().map((r) => r.id);
    ctx.label(`Reads here: ${ids.length}`);
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.read

Runs one add-on read on the model as the script has it so far and returns its answer (plain data; type it with read<T>). A plan's command is sent with ctx.editSteps when the script keeps it. A refusal fails the run with the add-on's words.

```ts
read<T = unknown>(id: string, input?: unknown): T
```

Topics: duct size, suggest duct size, panel loads, phase totals, read, computed, catalogue, feeder size

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const advice = ctx.read<{ suggested: { size: { width: number; height: number } } }>("mechanical.duct_size", { cfm: 1200, shape: "rect", height_mm: 305 });
    const { width, height } = advice.suggested.size;
    ctx.label(`Supply main ${Math.round(width / 25.4)}x${Math.round(height / 25.4)} for 1200 CFM`);
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.mm(width), units.mm(height)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(10) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(10) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.proposers

The proposers the model's add-ons offer: devices placed by a code's spacing or coverage (electrical.receptacles, plumbing.cleanouts…), each with what it places on.

```ts
proposers(): readonly { id: string; label: string; hosts: string }[]
```

Topics: proposers, what can propose, code spacing

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.label(ctx.proposers().map((p) => p.label).join(", "));
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.propose

Runs a proposer on rooms: ghost placements, each with the requirement it meets and the code clause, and a summary that says whether the rooms pass. Nothing is placed until ctx.acceptGhosts.

```ts
propose(proposerId: string, request: ProposerRequest): ProposerAnswer
```

Topics: receptacles, receptacle spacing, outlets, nec 210.52, propose devices, code spacing, cleanouts

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: units.ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }], thickness: units.in(4), height: units.ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const proposal = ctx.propose("electrical.receptacles", { typeId: "builtin:duplex-receptacle@1", roomIds: [bedroom, living], options: { mode: "dwelling", edition: "2023" } });
    ctx.acceptGhosts(proposal.ghosts, proposal.summary);
  },
});
```

</details>

## ctx.acceptGhosts

Places the ghosts kept (all, or a filtered list) as one edit on their level, each type pinned from the starter library when the model lacks it. Nothing is circuited or connected.

```ts
acceptGhosts(ghosts: readonly GhostPlacement[], label: string): void
```

Topics: accept, place proposed, keep some, receptacles

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: units.ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }], thickness: units.in(4), height: units.ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const proposal = ctx.propose("electrical.receptacles", { typeId: "builtin:duplex-receptacle@1", roomIds: [bedroom, living], options: { mode: "dwelling", edition: "2023" } });
    ctx.acceptGhosts(proposal.ghosts.filter((g) => g.roomId === bedroom), "Bedroom receptacles");
  },
});
```

</details>

---

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/units.md -->

# units

Typed lengths and other measures. Every length a kit function takes is a `units.*` value, never a bare number.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`units.mm`](#unitsmm): A length in millimetres.
- [`units.m`](#unitsm): A length in metres.
- [`units.in`](#unitsin): A length in inches.
- [`units.ft`](#unitsft): A length in feet.
- [`units.of`](#unitsof): A quantity of any kind in any unit the unit library knows (an airflow, a load, a pressure).
- [`units.in_`](#unitsin_): A measure's value in a unit (`units.in_(width, "in")` is 24 for a 24 in width).

## units.mm

A length in millimetres.

```ts
mm(value: number): Measure
```

Topics: units, metric, millimetre

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.mm(0), y: units.mm(0) }, { x: units.mm(6000), y: units.mm(0) }], thickness: units.mm(200) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## units.m

A length in metres.

```ts
m(value: number): Measure
```

Topics: units, metric, metre

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.m(0), y: units.m(0) }, { x: units.m(6), y: units.m(0) }], thickness: units.m(0.2) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## units.in

A length in inches.

```ts
in(value: number): Measure
```

Topics: units, imperial, inch

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.in(0), y: units.in(0) }, { x: units.in(240), y: units.in(0) }], thickness: units.in(8) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## units.ft

A length in feet.

```ts
ft(value: number): Measure
```

Topics: units, imperial, foot, feet

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(0) }], thickness: units.in(8) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## units.of

A quantity of any kind in any unit the unit library knows (an airflow, a load, a pressure).

```ts
of(kind: string, value: number, unit: string): Measure
```

Topics: units, airflow, cfm, quantity

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const tall = units.of("length", 3, "m");
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.m(0), y: units.m(0) }, { x: units.m(5), y: units.m(0) }], thickness: units.mm(150), height: tall });
  },
});
```

</details>

## units.in_

A measure's value in a unit (`units.in_(width, "in")` is 24 for a 24 in width).

```ts
in_(m: Measure, unit: string): number
```

Topics: units, convert, number

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const inches = Math.round(units.in_(v.width, "in"));
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: `${inches}`, category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box." + inches, b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/building.md -->

# building

Levels, grids, walls, doors, windows, floors, ceilings, roofs, stairs, rooms and spaces.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`building.walls`](#buildingwalls): Walls along the points, one per leg; `closed` joins the last point to the first.
- [`building.wall`](#buildingwall): One wall from `from` to `to`; returns its id. `height`, `top` and `base` as for building.walls: a partition run to the ceiling, an exterior wall up to the structure above.
- [`building.floor`](#buildingfloor): A floor slab with this outline (and optional stairwell/atrium `holes`) and `material`; returns its id.
- [`building.roof`](#buildingroof): A flat, single-slope shed, two-slope gable, or four-slope hip roof (`architecture.roof`) with optional `form`, `slopeRise`, `slopeDirectionDeg`, `baseOffset`, and `material`; returns its id.
- [`building.stair`](#buildingstair): A stair (`architecture.stair`) supporting straight runs, 90° L-shape, and 180° U-shape switchbacks with landings; returns its id.
- [`building.grid`](#buildinggrid): A structural column grid line (`grid`, e.g. `1`, `A`) drawn with Revit circular bubbles across every plan, RCP, and building section; returns its id.
- [`building.column`](#buildingcolumn): A structural or architectural column at a plan point; returns its id.
- [`building.curtainWall`](#buildingcurtainwall): A glazed architectural storefront / curtain wall from `from` to `to` with automatic 3D/plan mullions and optional `mullionMaterial`; returns its id.
- [`building.moveWall`](#buildingmovewall): Move a wall by a plan delta, carrying joined walls and collinear slab/ceiling/roof edges unless `disjoin: true`.
- [`building.moveOpening`](#buildingmoveopening): Slide a hosted door or window along its host wall by a plan delta (without moving the host wall).
- [`building.moveWallEnd`](#buildingmovewallend): Stretch or move one end of a wall (`"start" | "end"`) to a plan point, carrying joined corners unless `disjoin: true`.
- [`building.materials`](#buildingmaterials): List every material registered in the active add-ons (`kernel.material`), with visual and building-envelope thermal properties.
- [`building.assemblyThermal`](#buildingassemblythermal): Compute steady-state ISO 6946 / ASHRAE R-value and U-value of a layered wall/roof/floor assembly from registered `kernel.material` conductivities.
- [`building.setMaterial`](#buildingsetmaterial): Assign a registered material id (`building.materials()`) to one or more elements so both 2D plan poché and 3D textures reflect it.
- [`building.lock`](#buildinglock): Pin / lock elements so interactive selection and drags leave them alone.
- [`building.unlock`](#buildingunlock): Unpin / unlock previously locked elements.
- [`building.elements`](#buildingelements): Any kind the registry draws on a line (a beam, a grid line, a pack's own kind), by its id, along the points.
- [`building.door`](#buildingdoor): A door in a wall, its centre `along` the wall from its start; returns its id.
- [`building.window`](#buildingwindow): A window in a wall, its centre `along` the wall from its start, its bottom `sill` above the wall's floor (the type's sill, else 900 mm, when left out; the kernel refuses a sill that puts the head above the wall); returns its id.
- [`building.space`](#buildingspace): A space (room) with its number and name, on a level; returns its id.
- [`building.level`](#buildinglevel): A level at an elevation; returns its id.
- [`building.spaceInWalls`](#buildingspaceinwalls): A room found from the walls around a point: the kernel traces the enclosure and refuses an open room in words; returns the space's id.
- [`building.ceiling`](#buildingceiling): A ceiling on a level at a height above it (`form`: flat ACT grid, soffit with vertical fascia skirt, cloud, sloped, or open_to_structure) with optional `material` and `holes`; returns its id.
- [`building.room`](#buildingroom): A room (number, name, outline) on a level: what receptacle spacing, room schedules and room circuit templates read.
- [`building.surfacesAt`](#buildingsurfacesat): The floor or roof under an element or point, the ceiling and roof over it, and the structure above, each with its elevation and height above the floor (mm).
- [`building.levelSyncPlan`](#buildinglevelsyncplan): What matching the model's levels to a linked model's storeys would do (add, update, match, unchanged), changing nothing.
- [`building.syncLevels`](#buildingsynclevels): Makes the model's levels match a linked model's storeys as one edit: levels already at that height are matched and keep their names, new storeys become levels.

## building.walls

Walls along the points, one per leg; `closed` joins the last point to the first. A fixed `height`, or a `top`: `{ level, offset }` (up to a level; `topLevel` / `topOffset` say the same), "structure above" (the underside of the slab or deck over it), "ceiling", "roof" (sloped under a pitched roof), or `{ to, offset }`. The height then follows it. `base`: "slab below" (the top of the floor under it) or `{ offset }` off the level. Returns the chain (element(1) is the first wall).

```ts
walls(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: ChainSpec): ChainHandle
```

Topics: wall, walls, architecture, room, building outline, wall top, top level, floor to floor, tied to level, top, base, wall height, structure above, underside of slab, deck, ceiling, roof, sloped roof, top offset, base offset, attach top

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    // Exterior walls on Level 1 that run up to Level 2 and follow it if its elevation changes.
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(30) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(30) }], thickness: units.in(8), topLevel: "L2" });
    // A floor on Level 2, partitions run to its underside, and one 6 in under Level 2 standing on the slab below.
    building.floor(ctx, { level: "L2", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], thickness: units.in(8) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(20) }], thickness: units.in(5), top: "structure above" });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(20) }], thickness: units.in(5), top: { level: "L2", offset: units.in(-6) }, base: "slab below" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.wall

One wall from `from` to `to`; returns its id. `height`, `top` and `base` as for building.walls: a partition run to the ceiling, an exterior wall up to the structure above.

```ts
wall(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: WallSpec): string
```

Topics: wall, partition, one wall, top, structure above, ceiling, roof

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.floor(ctx, { level: "L2", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], thickness: units.in(8) });
    building.wall(ctx, { level: "L1", from: { x: units.ft(5), y: units.ft(2) }, to: { x: units.ft(5), y: units.ft(18) }, thickness: units.in(5), top: { to: "structure above", offset: units.in(-1) } });
  },
});
```

</details>

A floor slab with this outline (and optional stairwell/atrium `holes`) and `material`; returns its id.

```ts
floor(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: Omit<ChainSpec, "closed" | "topLevel" | "topOffset" | "top" | "base"> & { readonly holes?: readonly (readonly PlanPoint[])[] }): string
```

```ts
  },

```

</details>

## building.roof

A flat, single-slope shed, two-slope gable, or four-slope hip roof (`architecture.roof`) with optional `form`, `slopeRise`, `slopeDirectionDeg`, `baseOffset`, and `material`; returns its id.

```ts
roof(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: Omit<ChainSpec, "closed" | "topLevel" | "topOffset" | "top" | "base"> & { readonly form?: "flat" | "shed" | "gable" | "hip"; readonly slopeRise?: number; readonly slopeDirectionDeg?: number; readonly baseOffset?: Measure }): string
```

```ts
  },
});
```

## building.moveWall

Move a wall by a plan delta, carrying joined walls and collinear slab/ceiling/roof edges unless `disjoin: true`.

```ts
moveWall(ctx: ScriptContext, wallId: string, delta: PlanPoint, opts?: { readonly disjoin?: boolean }): void
```

Topics: wall, move, join, disjoin, architecture

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    building.moveWall(ctx, walls.element(1), { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(-2) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.moveOpening

Slide a hosted door or window along its host wall by a plan delta (without moving the host wall).

```ts
moveOpening(ctx: ScriptContext, openingId: string, delta: PlanPoint): void
```

Topics: door, window, opening, move, slide, architecture

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const d = building.door(ctx, { wall: walls.element(1), along: units.ft(8), width: units.in(36) });
    building.moveOpening(ctx, d, { x: units.ft(2), y: units.ft(0) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.moveWallEnd

Stretch or move one end of a wall (`"start" | "end"`) to a plan point, carrying joined corners unless `disjoin: true`.

```ts
moveWallEnd(ctx: ScriptContext, wallId: string, end: "start" | "end", to: PlanPoint, opts?: { readonly disjoin?: boolean }): void
```

Topics: wall, stretch, endpoint, corner, join, architecture

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    building.moveWallEnd(ctx, walls.element(1), "end", { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.materials

List every material registered in the active add-ons (`kernel.material`), with visual and building-envelope thermal properties.

```ts
materials(): readonly { readonly id: string; readonly name: string; readonly category?: string; readonly color: string; readonly pattern?: string; readonly thermalConductivityWPerMK?: number; readonly densityKgPerM3?: number; readonly shgc?: number }[]
```

Topics: material, color, texture, poche, thermal, envelope, architecture

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const mats = building.materials();
    if (mats.length === 0) throw new Error("expected architectural materials");
    ctx.report("Materials", { count: mats.length });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.assemblyThermal

Compute steady-state ISO 6946 / ASHRAE R-value and U-value of a layered wall/roof/floor assembly from registered `kernel.material` conductivities.

```ts
assemblyThermal(layers: readonly { readonly materialId: string; readonly thickness: Measure }[], opts?: { readonly includeAirFilms?: boolean }): AssemblyThermalSummary
```

Topics: envelope, thermal, r-value, u-value, insulation, energy, architecture

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const env = building.assemblyThermal([{ materialId: "architecture.brick_red", thickness: units.in(4) }, { materialId: "architecture.batt_insulation", thickness: units.in(5.5) }, { materialId: "architecture.gypsum_partition", thickness: units.in(0.625) }]);
    if (env.rImperial <= 0) throw new Error("expected positive R-value");
    ctx.report("Thermal", { rImperial: env.rImperial });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.setMaterial

Assign a registered material id (`building.materials()`) to one or more elements so both 2D plan poché and 3D textures reflect it.

```ts
setMaterial(ctx: ScriptContext, elementIds: string | readonly string[], materialId: string): void
```

Topics: material, color, texture, poche, wall, architecture

```ts
    building.setMaterial(ctx, walls.element(1), "architecture.brick_red");
  },
});
```

</details>

```ts
  },
```

</details>

```ts
  },

```

</details>

## building.elements

Any kind the registry draws on a line (a beam, a grid line, a pack's own kind), by its id, along the points.

```ts
  },
```


</details>

## building.window

A window in a wall, its centre `along` the wall from its start, its bottom `sill` above the wall's floor (the type's sill, else 900 mm, when left out; the kernel refuses a sill that puts the head above the wall); returns its id.

```ts
window(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: OpeningSpec): string
```

```ts
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.space

A space (room) with its number and name, on a level; returns its id. Loads, schedules and sizing read spaces.

```ts
space(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { level: string; number: string; name: string; outline?: PlanPoint[]; ceilingHeight?: Measure; occupants?: number; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: room, space, number, occupancy

```ts
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
```
