```ts
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.level

A level at an elevation; returns its id. Every level argument in the kit takes a level's id (this one, or one from ctx.model.levels()); the kit's helpers also take the name of exactly one level the script read (reads.levels: true), and refuse an unknown or shared name with the levels there are.

```ts
level(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { name: string; elevation: Measure; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: level, levels, storey, floor level, roof level

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.level(ctx, { name: "Level 3", elevation: units.ft(24) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.spaceInWalls

A room found from the walls around a point: the kernel traces the enclosure and refuses an open room in words; returns the space's id. It traces the walls in the script's model, so read them (reads.kinds: ["wall"]) unless the script draws them first; the kit stops with "you didn't read walls" otherwise.

```ts
spaceInWalls(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { level: string; inside: PlanPoint; number?: string; name?: string; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: rooms from walls, find rooms, room, space, trace rooms, enclosure

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    building.spaceInWalls(ctx, { level: "L1", inside: { x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(10) }, number: "101", name: "Office" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.ceiling

A ceiling on a level at a height above it (`form`: flat ACT grid, soffit with vertical fascia skirt, cloud, sloped, or open_to_structure) with optional `material` and `holes`; returns its id.

```ts
ceiling(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { level: string; outline: readonly PlanPoint[]; height: Measure; space?: string; form?: "flat" | "sloped" | "cloud" | "soffit" | "open_to_structure"; holes?: readonly (readonly PlanPoint[])[]; slope?: { directionDeg: number; pitch: number }; reference?: PlanPoint; typeId?: string; material?: string; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: ceiling, ceilings, ceiling height, sloped ceiling, soffit, cloud, acoustic tile, gypsum ceiling, reflected ceiling

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const office = building.spaceInWalls(ctx, { level: "L1", inside: { x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(10) }, number: "101", name: "Office" });
    const inside = [{ x: units.ft(1), y: units.ft(1) }, { x: units.ft(29), y: units.ft(1) }, { x: units.ft(29), y: units.ft(19) }, { x: units.ft(1), y: units.ft(19) }];
    const ceiling = building.ceiling(ctx, { level: "L1", space: office, form: "soffit", material: "architecture.gypsum_partition", outline: inside, height: units.ft(9) });
    ctx.report("Ceiling", ceiling);
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.room

A room (number, name, outline) on a level: what receptacle spacing, room schedules and room circuit templates read. Returns its id.

```ts
room(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { level: string; number: string; name: string; outline: readonly PlanPoint[]; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: room, rooms, room outline, room number

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Office", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(12), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(12), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.surfacesAt

The floor or roof under an element or point, the ceiling and roof over it, and the structure above, each with its elevation and height above the floor (mm). The model's own surfaces; linked models' slabs are the host's.

```ts
surfacesAt(ctx: ScriptContext, target: { element: string } | { at: PlanPoint; level?: string; elevation?: Measure }): SurfacesAt
```

Topics: surfaces, ceiling height, floor under, slab, roof over, structure above, clearance

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const here = building.surfacesAt(ctx, { at: { x: units.ft(5), y: units.ft(5) }, level: "L1" });
    ctx.label(here.ceiling ? `Ceiling at ${Math.round(here.ceiling.elevationMm)} mm` : "No ceiling over this point");
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.levelSyncPlan

What matching the model's levels to a linked model's storeys would do (add, update, match, unchanged), changing nothing. The storeys come from the host's link or the script's own values.

```ts
levelSyncPlan(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { reference: string; storeys: readonly { storeyId: string; name: string; elevation: Measure; levelId?: string }[] }): LevelSyncPlan
```

Topics: linked levels, sync levels, storeys, architect's model, levels from link

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const storeys = { reference: "arch-link", storeys: [{ storeyId: "s3", name: "Level 3", elevation: units.ft(26) }, { storeyId: "s4", name: "Roof", elevation: units.ft(39) }] };
    const plan = building.levelSyncPlan(ctx, storeys);
    if (plan.changes) building.syncLevels(ctx, storeys);
    else ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## building.syncLevels

Makes the model's levels match a linked model's storeys as one edit: levels already at that height are matched and keep their names, new storeys become levels.

```ts
syncLevels(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { reference: string; storeys: readonly { storeyId: string; name: string; elevation: Measure; levelId?: string }[] }): void
```

Topics: sync levels, linked levels, storeys

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.syncLevels(ctx, { reference: "arch-link", storeys: [{ storeyId: "s3", name: "Level 3", elevation: units.ft(26) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/routes.md -->

# routes

Duct, pipe and conduit runs: sizes, systems, slopes, where a run starts and ends, and connecting into a run.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`routes.rect`](#routesrect): A rectangular duct size.
- [`routes.round`](#routesround): A round duct size.
- [`routes.oval`](#routesoval): A flat-oval duct size.
- [`routes.pipe`](#routespipe): A pipe size: nominal diameter and material.
- [`routes.atConnector`](#routesatconnector): A route end at a placed part's connector (equipment, a fixture, a device).
- [`routes.atRunEnd`](#routesatrunend): A route end at an open end of a run (continue a duct or pipe).
- [`routes.along`](#routesalong): A duct, pipe, conduit or tray run through the points in order; the kernel places elbows, and `slope` makes a drain fall along it.
- [`routes.branch`](#routesbranch): A branch off a trunk: the kernel places the tap, tee or wye where it leaves.
- [`routes.drop`](#routesdrop): The route, then straight down (or up) at its last point to a height above another level; the kernel cuts the riser at each floor.
- [`routes.connectInto`](#routesconnectinto): Connects open ends (fixture connectors, run ends) into a run or the nearest one, with the system's fittings and slope.
- [`routes.setSystemGraphics`](#routessetsystemgraphics): Overrides a system's colour, line pattern, line weight, or repeating inline service code ("CW", "SAN", "G"; "" hides the code, null resets to default).
- [`routes.fittingTypes`](#routesfittingtypes): The fitting library routing places (the model's add-ons' families included): id, what it fits, shapes, parameters, and for pipe its services and joints.

## routes.rect

A rectangular duct size.

```ts
rect(width: Measure, height: Measure): RunSize
```

Topics: duct, rectangular, size

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(12), units.in(8)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.round

A round duct size.

```ts
round(diameter: Measure): RunSize
```

Topics: duct, round, size

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.round(units.in(10)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.oval

A flat-oval duct size.

```ts
oval(width: Measure, height: Measure): RunSize
```

Topics: duct, oval, size

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts

  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.pipe

A pipe size: nominal diameter and material.

```ts
pipe(nominal: Measure, material: PipeMaterial): RunSize
```

Topics: pipe, piping, size, water

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts

  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},

    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "pipe", size: routes.pipe(units.in(1), "copper"), system: { id: "dcw-1", kind: "domestic_cold_water" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.atConnector

A route end at a placed part's connector (equipment, a fixture, a device).

```ts
atConnector(partId: string, connectorId: string): RouteEnd
```

Topics: connect, equipment, connector, from

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.round(units.in(10)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, from: routes.atConnector("rtu-1", "supply"), points: [{ x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.atRunEnd

A route end at an open end of a run (continue a duct or pipe).

```ts
atRunEnd(elementId: string, port: "start" | "end" | string): RouteEnd
```

Topics: continue, extend, run end

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.round(units.in(10)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, from: routes.atRunEnd("run-1-s1", "end"), points: [{ x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.along

A duct, pipe, conduit or tray run through the points in order; the kernel places elbows, and `slope` makes a drain fall along it. A height change between two points rises straight up (`riseStyle: "vertical"`, the default) or on a slope of 60°, 45° or 22½° (`riseStyle: "60" | "45" | "22.5"`) where the run's fittings make that bend (PVC and cast iron drains have 1/6 and 1/16 bends; the kernel refuses an angle the fittings don't make, in words).

```ts
along(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: RouteSpec): RouteHandle
```

Topics: route, duct, pipe, run, slope, drain, sanitary, gravity, conduit, rise, 60 degree, 22.5 degree, offset

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "pipe", size: routes.pipe(units.in(3), "pvc"), system: { id: "san-1", kind: "sanitary" }, height: units.ft(-1), slope: { rise: units.in(0.25), per: units.ft(1) }, points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(40), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.branch

A branch off a trunk: the kernel places the tap, tee or wye where it leaves.

```ts
branch(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: RouteSpec & { trunk: string; face?: "top" | "bottom" }): RouteHandle
```

Topics: branch, tee, tap, wye, takeoff

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const main = routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(16), units.in(10)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(40), y: units.ft(0) }] });
    routes.branch(ctx, { trunk: main.segment(1), level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.round(units.in(8)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, points: [{ x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(10) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.drop

The route, then straight down (or up) at its last point to a height above another level; the kernel cuts the riser at each floor.

```ts
drop(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: RouteSpec & { toLevel: string; heightAbove: Measure }): RouteHandle
```

Topics: riser, drop, vertical, stack

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.drop(ctx, { level: "L2", toLevel: "L1", heightAbove: units.ft(1), domain: "pipe", size: routes.pipe(units.in(2), "copper"), system: { id: "dcw-1", kind: "domestic_cold_water" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(5), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.connectInto

Connects open ends (fixture connectors, run ends) into a run or the nearest one, with the system's fittings and slope.

```ts
connectInto(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { from: { elementId: string; port: string }[]; into: string; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: connect fixtures, drain, into, auto connect, many fixtures

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.connectInto(ctx, { from: [{ elementId: "wc-1", port: "waste" }, { elementId: "lav-1", port: "waste" }], into: "nearest" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.setSystemGraphics

Overrides a system's colour, line pattern, line weight, or repeating inline service code ("CW", "SAN", "G"; "" hides the code, null resets to default).

```ts
setSystemGraphics(ctx: ScriptContext, systemId: string, changes: { colour?: string | null; pattern?: SystemLinePattern | null; weight?: SystemLineWeight | null; lineCode?: string | null }): void
```

Topics: system graphics, line pattern, line weight, line code, schematic, colour, piping style

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "pipe", size: routes.pipe(units.in(4), "pvc"), system: { id: "san-1", kind: "sanitary" }, height: units.ft(-1), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(40), y: units.ft(0) }] });
    routes.setSystemGraphics(ctx, "san-1", { pattern: "solid", weight: "medium", lineCode: "SAN" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.fittingTypes

The fitting library routing places (the model's add-ons' families included): id, what it fits, shapes, parameters, and for pipe its services and joints. Use an id with swap_fitting or a system's design.

```ts
fittingTypes(ctx: ScriptContext, filter?: { domain?: "duct" | "pipe"; service?: "water" | "drainage" | "vent" | "gas" }): readonly FittingFamily[]
```

Topics: fitting types, fitting library, elbows, takeoffs, pipe fittings, catalogue

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const elbows = routes.fittingTypes(ctx, { domain: "duct" }).filter((f) => f.fittingTypes.includes("elbow"));
    ctx.label(`Duct elbows: ${elbows.map((f) => f.name).join(", ")}`);
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/equipment.md -->

# equipment

Placing parts (equipment, fixtures, devices) by type, and their connectors.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`equipment.place`](#equipmentplace): Places one part (equipment, a fixture, a device) on a level; its connectors are route ends (`placed.connector("supply")`).
- [`equipment.hostOnWall`](#equipmenthostonwall): Re-hosts existing placed parts flush onto a wall finish face (`wall_face` host), moving and orienting each part onto the finish face (`"nearest"` snaps each part to its closest wall) so wall-anchored symbols clear the wall thickness and follow future wall edits.
- [`equipment.controlZone`](#equipmentcontrolzone): Binds switches (single-pole, 3-way/4-way travelers), 0-10V dimmers, occupancy or daylight sensors to the lighting fixtures or controlled receptacles they govern under one lowercase switch-leg letter (`"a"`, `"b"`), control wiring protocol (`"line_voltage"`, `"0-10v"`, `"dali"`, `"low_voltage"`, `"wireless"`), and optional emergency lighting mode (`"none"`, `"unswitched"`, `"switched"` UL 924).

## equipment.place

Places one part (equipment, a fixture, a device) on a level; its connectors are route ends (`placed.connector("supply")`). Pass `onWall` (`{ wall, along?, side?, toward?, offset? }` or `"nearest"`) to mount wall-hosted devices flush on the wall finish face with local `+Y` into the room so annotative symbols stay outside the wall thickness and follow wall edits.

```ts
place(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { level: string; type: string; at?: PlanPoint; height?: Measure; rotationDeg?: number; mark?: string; values?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>; onSlab?: string; onWall?: WallMountSpec | "nearest"; zone?: string; id?: string }): PlacedPart
```

Topics: place equipment, rooftop unit, rtu, water heater, panel, fixture, device, wall mount, wall host, onWall, receptacle, switch, connect equipment, library part, built-in part

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const rtu = equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: "acme.rtu.10t", at: { x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(10) }, mark: "RTU-1" });
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(20), units.in(12)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, from: rtu.connector("supply"), points: [{ x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## equipment.hostOnWall

Re-hosts existing placed parts flush onto a wall finish face (`wall_face` host), moving and orienting each part onto the finish face (`"nearest"` snaps each part to its closest wall) so wall-anchored symbols clear the wall thickness and follow future wall edits.

```ts
hostOnWall(ctx: ScriptContext, partIds: string | readonly string[], onWall?: WallMountSpec | "nearest", opts?: { maxDistance?: Measure }): readonly { partId: string; wallId: string; side: 1 | -1; stationMm: number }[]
```

Topics: wall host, wall face, rehost, hostOnWall, receptacle, switch, flush on wall, mount on wall

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const w = building.wall(ctx, { level: "L1", from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(0) } });
    const r = equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: "builtin:duplex-receptacle@1", at: { x: units.ft(6), y: units.ft(0.5) }, height: units.in(18), mark: "R-1" });
    equipment.hostOnWall(ctx, r.id, { wall: w, toward: { x: units.ft(6), y: units.ft(4) } });
  },
});
```

</details>

## equipment.controlZone

Binds switches (single-pole, 3-way/4-way travelers), 0-10V dimmers, occupancy or daylight sensors to the lighting fixtures or controlled receptacles they govern under one lowercase switch-leg letter (`"a"`, `"b"`), control wiring protocol (`"line_voltage"`, `"0-10v"`, `"dali"`, `"low_voltage"`, `"wireless"`), and optional emergency lighting mode (`"none"`, `"unswitched"`, `"switched"` UL 924).

```ts
controlZone(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { leg: string; controllers: readonly (string | PlacedPart)[]; loads: readonly (string | PlacedPart)[]; protocol?: "line_voltage" | "0-10v" | "dali" | "low_voltage" | "wireless"; emergencyMode?: "none" | "unswitched" | "switched" }): void
```

Topics: switching, switch leg, 0-10v, dimmer, occupancy sensor, controls, lighting control, controlled receptacle, emergency lighting, ul 924

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const sw = equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: "builtin:switch-dimmer@1", at: { x: units.ft(2), y: units.ft(0) }, mark: "SD-1" });
    const lt = equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: "builtin:troffer-2x4-led@1", at: { x: units.ft(8), y: units.ft(8) }, mark: "F1" });
    equipment.controlZone(ctx, { leg: "a", controllers: [sw], loads: [lt], protocol: "0-10v", emergencyMode: "switched" });
  },
});
```

</details>

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/parts.md -->

# parts

Making part types: a part's bodies, connectors and parameters.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`parts.part`](#partspart): Start one size of a custom part (equipment, a fixture, a device): declare optional `hosting` (`"wall_face"` snaps flush onto walls and auto-rotates, `"ceiling"`, `"floor"`, `"free"`), add bodies, connectors and annotative plan symbols, then build().
- [`parts.faces`](#partsfaces): The faces a connector can go on: top, bottom, front, back, left, right.
- [`parts.rect`](#partsrect): A rectangle profile (width along the view's first axis, height along its second), centred unless center moves it; corners filleted or chamfered.
- [`parts.circle`](#partscircle): A circle profile of a diameter, centred unless center moves it.
- [`parts.polygon`](#partspolygon): Any closed polygon profile of fixed corners (wound either way); corners filleted or chamfered.
- [`parts.views`](#partsviews): The views a profile is drawn in: plan (x right, y up; bodies go up), front (y right, z up; bodies go toward the front, +x), side (x right, z up; bodies go left, +y).
- [`parts.starterTypes`](#partsstartertypes): The starter library's part types in every discipline, filtered by words in the family, type, category or id.
- [`parts.refreshBuiltins`](#partsrefreshbuiltins): Upgrades stale built-in part types already pinned in an existing model to the latest library symbols (`mode: "symbols"`, default) or full definitions (`mode: "full"`) as one atomic edit, leaving placed parts and custom types untouched.

## parts.part

Start one size of a custom part (equipment, a fixture, a device): declare optional `hosting` (`"wall_face"` snaps flush onto walls and auto-rotates, `"ceiling"`, `"floor"`, `"free"`), add bodies, connectors and annotative plan symbols, then build().

```ts
part(name: string, start: { type: string; category: PartCategory; description?: string; hosting?: "free" | "wall_face" | "ceiling" | "floor"; tagFields?: string[] }): PartBuilder
```

Topics: custom part, equipment, rooftop unit, rtu, water heater, panel, family, wall_face, hosting

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.faces

The faces a connector can go on: top, bottom, front, back, left, right.

```ts
faces: readonly ("top" | "bottom" | "front" | "back" | "left" | "right")[]
```

Topics: face, connector, side

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    for (const face of parts.faces) if (face === "top") b.connector(face, { id: "out", label: "Outlet", domain: "duct", systemKind: "supply_air", shape: "round", diameter: units.in(10), endType: "mechanical.slip" });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.rect

A rectangle profile (width along the view's first axis, height along its second), centred unless center moves it; corners filleted or chamfered.

```ts
rect(width: Length, height: Length, opts?: { center?: [Length, Length]; fillet?: Length; chamfer?: Length }): Profile
```

Topics: profile, rectangle, rounded corners, fillet, chamfer

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Cabinet", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.extrude(parts.rect(v.width, units.in(18), { fillet: units.in(1) }), { to: units.in(30) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.cab.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.circle

A circle profile of a diameter, centred unless center moves it.

```ts
circle(diameter: Length, opts?: { center?: [Length, Length] }): Profile
```

Topics: profile, circle, round, tank

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Tank", { type: "24", category: "plumbing_fixture" });
    b.extrude(parts.circle(v.width), { to: units.in(48) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.tank.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.polygon

Any closed polygon profile of fixed corners (wound either way); corners filleted or chamfered. Use for curbs, hoods, brackets, odd housings.

```ts
polygon(points: [Length, Length][], opts?: { fillet?: Length; chamfer?: Length }): Profile
```

Topics: profile, polygon, outline, custom shape, hood

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Hood", { type: "48", category: "mechanical_equipment" });
    b.extrude(parts.polygon([[units.in(0), units.in(0)], [units.in(48), units.in(0)], [units.in(48), units.in(24)], [units.in(12), units.in(36)], [units.in(0), units.in(36)]], { chamfer: units.in(2) }), { on: "side", from: units.in(-12), to: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.hood.48", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.views

The views a profile is drawn in: plan (x right, y up; bodies go up), front (y right, z up; bodies go toward the front, +x), side (x right, z up; bodies go left, +y).

```ts
views: readonly ("plan" | "front" | "side")[]
```

Topics: view, plane, orientation, which way

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Plate", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    for (const view of parts.views) if (view === "front") b.extrude(parts.rect(v.width, units.in(12)), { on: view, to: units.in(0.5) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.plate.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.starterTypes

The starter library's part types in every discipline, filtered by words in the family, type, category or id. Place one with equipment.place by its id (the type is pinned into the model with the placement).

```ts
starterTypes(ctx: ScriptContext, words?: string): readonly StarterType[]
```

Topics: starter library, part types, built-in parts, catalogue, panelboard, receptacle type

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const panel = parts.starterTypes(ctx, "panelboard")[0];
    if (!panel) throw new Error("No starter panelboard");
    equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: panel.id, at: { x: units.ft(1), y: units.ft(1) }, mark: "LP-1" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.refreshBuiltins

Upgrades stale built-in part types already pinned in an existing model to the latest library symbols (`mode: "symbols"`, default) or full definitions (`mode: "full"`) as one atomic edit, leaving placed parts and custom types untouched.

```ts
refreshBuiltins(ctx: ScriptContext, opts?: { typeIds?: readonly string[]; mode?: "symbols" | "full" }): readonly { typeId: string; familyName: string; typeName: string }[]
```

Topics: refresh symbols, upgrade part types, built-in symbols, annotative symbols, stale symbols, refreshBuiltins

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const updated = parts.refreshBuiltins(ctx);
    ctx.report("refreshed", updated.length);
  },
});
```

</details>

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/part-builder.md -->

# PartBuilder

The builder `parts.part()` returns: boxes, extrusions, sweeps, connectors and parameters on one part type.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`PartBuilder.planSymbol`](#partbuilderplansymbol): Adds 2D plan symbol primitives (`circle`, `rect`, `line`, `arc`, `polyline`, `text`) with `units: "paper"`, `minPaperMm` floors, `fill: "mask" | "solid"`, conditional `when` parameter rules (e.g. emergency battery shading), `mask: true` text wipeouts, and `upright` / `uprightOffset` wall-safe subscripts.
- [`PartBuilder.param`](#partbuilderparam): A type parameter; pass the returned dimension to a body or connector and it follows the parameter on every size.
- [`PartBuilder.box`](#partbuilderbox): A box standing on the base.
- [`PartBuilder.cylinder`](#partbuildercylinder): A cylinder along x, y or z (z stands on the base): a tank, a water heater, a fan.
- [`PartBuilder.transition`](#partbuildertransition): A taper along x between two rectangular openings: width and height both change (fromHeight / toHeight), and offset moves the outlet.
- [`PartBuilder.connector`](#partbuilderconnector): A connector on a face, pointing out of it: duct, pipe, gas or electrical, with its system kind and size.
- [`PartBuilder.build`](#partbuilderbuild): The part-type definition, checked with the kernel's schema and part rules (a problem fails here, in the kernel's words).
- [`PartBuilder.check`](#partbuildercheck): `build` plus the kernel's connector placement warnings (a part with warnings still saves).
- [`PartBuilder.extrude`](#partbuilderextrude): Push a profile (any outline, with holes) straight out of its view between from and to; cut: true removes material instead.
- [`PartBuilder.cut`](#partbuildercut): Remove material with a profile pushed out of its view: openings, recesses, holes through a casing.
- [`PartBuilder.revolve`](#partbuilderrevolve): Turn a profile about a line drawn in the same view (default 360 degrees): bells, domes, nozzles, round tanks with heads.
- [`PartBuilder.sweep`](#partbuildersweep): Carry a profile along straights and bends drawn in a view: elbows, offsets, coil returns, handrails.
- [`PartBuilder.loft`](#partbuilderloft): A solid through two or more sections, each a profile on its own plane: square-to-round transitions, hoods, cones, wye legs.
- [`PartBuilder.pattern`](#partbuilderpattern): Repeat earlier bodies (by id, or "last") in a line or around an axis: coil fins, louvre blades, bolt circles, breaker rows.
- [`PartBuilder.mirror`](#partbuildermirror): A mirrored copy of earlier bodies across the plane square to an axis (at along it; default the centre).
- [`PartBuilder.importBody`](#partbuilderimportbody): A body from a vendor's glTF or OBJ library file, pinned by its content hash (read sanitized and size-capped by the host); at places its origin, turn turns it about z.
- [`PartBuilder.symbol`](#partbuildersymbol): Plan symbol drawn instead of the solid at chosen detail levels: shapes, lines, texts, optional paper-space scaling (`units: "paper"`), minimum plotted paper floor (`minPaperMm` on model-size symbols so true-scale equipment stays legible when zoomed out), opaque white mask (`mask: true`), solid black fill (`filled: true`), and pen weight.
- [`PartBuilder.symbolRef`](#partbuildersymbolref): Attach a registered plan symbol from SYMBOL_POINT (e.g. electrical.plan_duplex, electrical.plan_gfci, electrical.plan_switch, electrical.plan_occ_sensor, electrical.plan_downlight_em) at chosen detail levels.
- [`PartBuilder.clearance`](#partbuilderclearance): Space kept clear in front of a face (service access, combustibles, working space); never solid, checked by clash.
- [`PartBuilder.connectorAt`](#partbuilderconnectorat): A connector at an exact point of the part (x to the front, y to the left, z up), facing out of a face: an outlet on a section, a stub on a hood.
- [`PartBuilder.instanceParam`](#partbuilderinstanceparam): A value each placed copy carries for itself (a panel's name, its mains), with an optional default; shown in properties and schedules, not in the shape.
- [`PartBuilder.draft`](#partbuilderdraft): The definition as built so far, unchecked.

## PartBuilder.planSymbol

Adds 2D plan symbol primitives (`circle`, `rect`, `line`, `arc`, `polyline`, `text`) with `units: "paper"`, `minPaperMm` floors, `fill: "mask" | "solid"`, conditional `when` parameter rules (e.g. emergency battery shading), `mask: true` text wipeouts, and `upright` / `uprightOffset` wall-safe subscripts.

```ts
planSymbol(primitives: readonly SymbolPrimitive[]): PartBuilder
```

Topics: plan symbol, annotative, paper units, minPaperMm, conditional symbol, when, mask, circle, wall_face

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Wall Sensor", { type: "24V", category: "electrical_device", hosting: "wall_face" });
    b.box({ length: units.in(3), width: units.in(1), height: units.in(4.5) });
    b.planSymbol([{ kind: "line", from: [0, 0], to: [0, 1.4], pen: "medium", units: "paper" }, { kind: "circle", center: [0, 2.8], radius: 1.4, fill: "mask", pen: "medium", units: "paper" }, { kind: "text", at: [0, 2.8], text: "WS", heightMm: 1.5, mask: true, units: "paper" }]);
    ctx.parts.define("acme.wall_sensor.24v", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.param

A type parameter; pass the returned dimension to a body or connector and it follows the parameter on every size.

```ts
param(name: string, spec: { label: string; value: Measure | number | string | boolean; unit?: string }): Dim
```

Topics: parameter, size, formula, type parameter

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    const w = b.param("width", { label: "Width", value: v.width });
    b.box({ length: w, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.box

A box standing on the base. The first body is the part's envelope: connectors go on its faces.

```ts
box(size: { length: Length; width: Length; height: Length }, at?: { x?: Length; y?: Length; base?: Length } & BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

Topics: box, casing, cabinet, rooftop unit, panel, body

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.box({ length: units.in(6), width: units.in(6), height: units.in(4) }, { base: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.cylinder

A cylinder along x, y or z (z stands on the base): a tank, a water heater, a fan.

```ts
cylinder(spec: { diameter: Length; length: Length; axis: "x" | "y" | "z" }, at?: { x?: Length; y?: Length; z?: Length } & BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

```ts
    b.cylinder({ diameter: units.in(22), length: units.in(60), axis: "z" });
    b.connector("top", { id: "cw", label: "Cold water", domain: "pipe", systemKind: "domestic_cold_water", shape: "round", diameter: units.in(0.75), offset: [units.in(-4), units.in(0)], endType: "plumbing_gas.sweat" });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.wh.50", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.transition

A taper along x between two rectangular openings: width and height both change (fromHeight / toHeight), and offset moves the outlet. A loft underneath.

```ts
transition(spec: { length: Length; fromWidth: Length; toWidth: Length; height?: Length; fromHeight?: Length; toHeight?: Length; offset?: [Length, Length] } & BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

Topics: transition, reducer, taper, offset transition

```ts

export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Transition", { type: "24x16-12x8", category: "duct_accessory" });
    b.transition({ length: units.in(18), fromWidth: v.width, toWidth: units.in(12), fromHeight: units.in(16), toHeight: units.in(8) });
    b.connector("back", { id: "in", label: "Inlet", domain: "duct", systemKind: "supply_air", shape: "rect", width: v.width, height: units.in(16), endType: "mechanical.slip" });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.tr.24x16", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.connector

A connector on a face, pointing out of it: duct, pipe, gas or electrical, with its system kind and size. Faces are the first body's (envelope) or, with of "body", the box around everything built.

```ts
connector(face: Face, c: ConnectorSpec & { offset?: [Length, Length] }, of?: "envelope" | "body"): PartBuilder
```

Topics: connector, duct connection, pipe connection, gas, electrical connection, power

```ts
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.connector("top", { id: "supply", label: "Supply", domain: "duct", systemKind: "supply_air", shape: "rect", width: units.in(12), height: units.in(8), endType: "mechanical.slip" });
    b.connector("left", { id: "power", label: "Power", domain: "electrical", systemKind: "power", shape: "none" });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

```ts
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.check

`build` plus the kernel's connector placement warnings (a part with warnings still saves).

```ts
check(): { definition: PartTypeDefinition; warnings: readonly string[] }
```

Topics: check, warnings

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    const checked = b.check();
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", checked.definition);
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.extrude

Push a profile (any outline, with holes) straight out of its view between from and to; cut: true removes material instead.

```ts
extrude(profile: Profile, spec: { on?: View; at?: Length; from?: Length; to: Length } & BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

Topics: extrude, profile, hole, curb, casing, body

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Curb", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.extrude(parts.rect(v.width, units.in(48)).hole(parts.rect(units.in(20), units.in(44))), { to: units.in(14), material: "Galvanized steel" });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.curb.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.cut

Remove material with a profile pushed out of its view: openings, recesses, holes through a casing.

```ts
cut(profile: Profile, spec: { on?: View; at?: Length; from?: Length; to: Length } & BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

Topics: cut, opening, hole, recess, subtract, boolean

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts

export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.cut(parts.rect(units.in(10), units.in(8), { center: [units.in(0), units.in(6)] }), { on: "front", from: units.in(0), to: units.in(20) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.revolve

Turn a profile about a line drawn in the same view (default 360 degrees): bells, domes, nozzles, round tanks with heads.

```ts
revolve(profile: Profile, spec: { on?: View; at?: Length; axis: [[Length, Length], [Length, Length]]; angle?: number; startAngle?: number } & BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

```ts
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Bell", { type: "12", category: "generic" });
    b.revolve(parts.polygon([[units.in(4), units.in(0)], [units.in(6), units.in(0)], [units.in(4.5), units.in(8)], [units.in(4), units.in(8)]]), { on: "front", axis: [[units.in(0), units.in(0)], [units.in(0), units.in(1)]] });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.bell.12", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.sweep

Carry a profile along straights and bends drawn in a view: elbows, offsets, coil returns, handrails. The profile is drawn across the path where it starts.

```ts
sweep(profile: Profile, path: SweepPath, opts?: BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

Topics: sweep, elbow, bend, offset, fitting, path

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Elbow", { type: "10 in 90", category: "duct_accessory" });
    b.sweep(parts.circle(units.in(10)), { on: "plan", at: units.in(12), start: [units.in(0), units.in(0)], heading: "right", segments: [{ straight: units.in(4) }, { bend: { radius: units.in(15), angle: 90, turn: "left" } }, { straight: units.in(4) }] });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.elbow.10", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.loft

A solid through two or more sections, each a profile on its own plane: square-to-round transitions, hoods, cones, wye legs.

```ts
loft(sections: { profile: Profile; on?: View; at: Length }[], opts?: BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

Topics: loft, square to round, transition, taper, wye, cone

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Square to round", { type: "24-16", category: "duct_accessory" });
    b.loft([{ profile: parts.rect(v.width, v.width), at: units.in(0) }, { profile: parts.circle(units.in(16)), at: units.in(18) }]);
    ctx.parts.define("acme.s2r.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.pattern

Repeat earlier bodies (by id, or "last") in a line or around an axis: coil fins, louvre blades, bolt circles, breaker rows.

```ts
pattern(ids: string[] | "last", spec: { along: "x" | "y" | "z"; count: number; spacing: Length } | { around: "x" | "y" | "z"; count: number; angle?: number; center?: [Length, Length, Length] }, opts?: { id?: string }): PartBuilder
```

Topics: pattern, repeat, array, louvre, fins, bolt circle

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.extrude(parts.rect(units.in(0.5), units.in(12)), { from: units.in(12), to: units.in(13), id: "blade" });
    b.pattern(["blade"], { along: "x", count: 6, spacing: units.in(3) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.mirror

A mirrored copy of earlier bodies across the plane square to an axis (at along it; default the centre).

```ts
mirror(ids: string[] | "last", spec: { across: "x" | "y" | "z"; at?: Length }, opts?: { id?: string }): PartBuilder
```

Topics: mirror, symmetric, copy, opposite side

```ts
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.extrude(parts.rect(units.in(2), units.in(2), { center: [units.in(8), units.in(4)] }), { from: units.in(12), to: units.in(14), id: "foot" });

  },

```

</details>

## PartBuilder.importBody

A body from a vendor's glTF or OBJ library file, pinned by its content hash (read sanitized and size-capped by the host); at places its origin, turn turns it about z.

```ts
importBody(body: ImportedBodyRef, at?: { x?: Length; y?: Length; z?: Length; turn?: number }, opts?: BodyOptions): PartBuilder
```

Topics: import, gltf, obj, vendor model, manufacturer model, 3d file

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Vendor fan", { type: "24", category: "mechanical_equipment" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: v.width, height: units.in(2) });
    b.importBody({ fileId: "library-file-1", format: "gltf", contentHash: "sha256:demo", mmPerUnit: 1000, upAxis: "y" }, { z: units.in(2) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.fan.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.symbol

Plan symbol drawn instead of the solid at chosen detail levels: shapes, lines, texts, optional paper-space scaling (`units: "paper"`), minimum plotted paper floor (`minPaperMm` on model-size symbols so true-scale equipment stays legible when zoomed out), opaque white mask (`mask: true`), solid black fill (`filled: true`), and pen weight. Levels without a symbol fall back to the solid seen from above.

```ts
symbol(levels: DetailLevel | DetailLevel[], draw: { shapes?: Profile[]; lines?: [[Length, Length], [Length, Length]][]; texts?: { at: [Length, Length]; text: string; heightMm?: number; anchor?: "start" | "middle" | "end" }[]; units?: "model" | "paper"; minPaperMm?: number; pen?: "thin" | "medium" | "wide" | "heavy"; filled?: boolean; mask?: boolean }, view?: "plan" | "below"): PartBuilder
```

Topics: symbol, plan symbol, custom symbol, paper scale, annotative, minPaperMm, minimum paper height, mask, fill, detail level, coarse, fine, drafting

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.symbol(["coarse", "medium"], { units: "paper", mask: true, shapes: [parts.circle(units.mm(3.2))], lines: [[[units.mm(-0.65), units.mm(-2.5)], [units.mm(-0.65), units.mm(1.45)]], [[units.mm(0.65), units.mm(-2.5)], [units.mm(0.65), units.mm(1.45)]]], texts: [{ at: [units.mm(2.2), units.mm(1.7)], text: "WP", heightMm: 1.7, anchor: "start" }] });
    b.symbol("fine", { units: "model", minPaperMm: 4, mask: true, shapes: [parts.rect(units.in(24), units.in(24))] });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.wp_receptacle", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.symbolRef

```ts
symbolRef(levels: DetailLevel | DetailLevel[], symbolId: string, view?: "plan" | "below"): PartBuilder
```

```ts
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.symbolRef(["coarse", "medium", "fine"], "electrical.plan_gfci");
    ctx.parts.define("acme.gfci_custom", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

</details>

## PartBuilder.instanceParam

A value each placed copy carries for itself (a panel's name, its mains), with an optional default; shown in properties and schedules, not in the shape.

```ts
instanceParam(name: string, spec: { label: string; kind: "text" | "number" | "boolean" | "choice"; default?: string | number | boolean; unit?: string; choices?: string[] }): PartBuilder
```

Topics: instance parameter, per copy, panel name, property

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    b.instanceParam("panel_name", { label: "Panel name", kind: "text", default: "LP-1" });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## PartBuilder.draft

The definition as built so far, unchecked.

```ts
draft(): PartTypeDefinition
```

Topics: draft

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    const draft = b.draft();
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", { ...draft, description: "A drafted box" });
  },
});
```

</details>

---

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/documents.md -->

# documents

Views, sheets, schedules, tags, notes, dimensions and the rest of a drawing set.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`documents.sheet`](#documentssheet): A new sheet (number, name, title block); returns its id.
- [`documents.setSheet`](#documentssetsheet): Changes a sheet's number, name, title block or fields.
- [`documents.planView`](#documentsplanview): A floor plan of one level (for a discipline, scale, detailLevel, symbolScale, showLineCodes, and per-category/service overrides including singleLineBelow); returns the view's id.
- [`documents.setView`](#documentssetview): Changes a view's detail level (coarse/medium/fine), visual style, annotative `symbolScale` (0.5–3.0), inline service codes, scale, discipline, or per-category/service graphics overrides (including singleLineBelow).
- [`documents.ceilingView`](#documentsceilingview): A reflected ceiling plan of one level; returns the view's id.
- [`documents.sectionView`](#documentssectionview): A vertical building section cut from `from` to `to` (direction +1 left / -1 right, depth default 20 ft); supports annotative `headExt`/`tailExt`, Revit `splitGap` break, explicit `crop`, and `levelLeftExtMm`/`levelRightExtMm` datum extensions.
- [`documents.elevationView`](#documentselevationview): An interior or exterior elevation looking from `from..to` (direction +1 left / -1 right, depth default 20 ft); its live elevation marker (circle + pointer arrow with auto-updating detail#/sheet# head) prints automatically on overlapping plans.
- [`documents.enlargedPlan`](#documentsenlargedplan): A Revit-style enlarged plan in one step: creates a cropped plan view on the same level at enlarged scale (default 1/4" or 1/2" = 1'-0") AND places a live parametric callout bubble on the parent plan whose detail#/sheet# head auto-updates when the enlarged plan moves sheets.
- [`documents.callout`](#documentscallout): Places a live parametric callout box + split head bubble on a view referencing any existing enlarged plan, 2D detail, section, or elevation view.
- [`documents.setCrop`](#documentssetcrop): Sets a view's crop box in typed units, toggles cropView/showCropBox, or adjusts section/elevation far clip depth, level datum extensions (`levelLeftExtMm`/`levelRightExtMm`), and section mark `headExt`/`tailExt`/`splitGap`.
- [`documents.duplicateView`](#documentsduplicateview): A copy of a view (another discipline's plan of the same level); returns the new id.
- [`documents.place`](#documentsplace): Puts a view (a plan, a schedule, a detail) on a sheet at a point (its centre, from the sheet's lower-left corner), with optional scale and viewport title offset/rule length; returns the viewport's id.
- [`documents.setViewportTitle`](#documentssetviewporttitle): Moves a placed viewport's title block on its sheet (`offset`) and/or changes the horizontal title underline length (`ruleLength`, or `null` to reset).
- [`documents.editSchedule`](#documentseditschedule): Edits a list schedule view in one undo step: add, move, remove or rename columns, filter, sort, group, totals (an equipment schedule's sort, a fixture schedule's DFU total).
- [`documents.schedule`](#documentsschedule): A schedule view; returns its id.
- [`documents.tag`](#documentstag): A tag on one element in a plan view (its mark, size or the right text for its kind), with a leader; returns the tag's id.
- [`documents.moveTag`](#documentsmovetag): Moves an existing tag in a plan view to a clear position (and optionally toggles its leader).
- [`documents.planLabels`](#documentsplanlabels): Returns every rendered text label on a plan view (paper mm coordinates and bounding boxes) plus any overlapping pairs, so scripts can verify legibility and move colliding tags.
- [`documents.dimension`](#documentsdimension): A dimension between two points in a view, tied to elements with refs so it follows them; returns its id.
- [`documents.tagStyle`](#documentstagstyle): A new tag style: field lines, box, orientation, what it applies to, and an arrow along the run (`arrow: "down_slope"` points downhill on the view's paper, `"up_slope"` uphill; level pipe shows none); returns its id.
- [`documents.setTagStyle`](#documentssettagstyle): Changes a tag style's look: lines, box, orientation, applies-to, mask, textStyleId or its arrow (`arrow: "none"` removes it).
- [`documents.textStyle`](#documentstextstyle): Creates a model-wide Text Type (font family, paper cap height, bold/italic/uppercase, opaque or transparent background mask, default drawing roles) so part marks, circuit labels, tags, dimensions and room labels stay unified and readable over crossing lines.
- [`documents.setTextStyle`](#documentssettextstyle): Updates an existing model-wide Text Type (size, font family, bold/italic/uppercase, opaque background mask, color, or default drawing roles).
- [`documents.deleteTextStyle`](#documentsdeletetextstyle): Deletes a model-wide Text Type by id.
- [`documents.flipWireArc`](#documentsflipwirearc): Flips (or explicitly sets) which side an automatic circuit or switch-leg arc bows toward on a plan view.
- [`documents.setCircuitGraphics`](#documentssetcircuitgraphics): Sets a plan view's circuit and switch-leg drawing style (`showCircuits: false` makes a dedicated controls schematic plan), home runs, switch-leg letters, and ANSI/NECA 100 wire hash marks (`home_runs`, `home_runs_and_switch_legs`, or `all_runs`) while keeping existing wire waypoints and home-run offsets intact.
- [`documents.setSwitchLegLabelOffset`](#documentssetswitchleglabeloffset): Repositions (or resets with `null`) one lowercase switch-leg letter (`"a"`, `"b"`) relative to its device anchor on a plan view.
- [`documents.setMwbcGroup`](#documentssetmwbcgroup): Groups (or splits with `null`) branch circuits on the same panel into a shared-neutral Multi-Wire Branch Circuit (MWBC, NEC 210.4) drawn as one multi-arrowhead combined home run with shared neutral hash marks.
- [`documents.setWirePath`](#documentssetwirepath): Pins one or more spline/orthogonal control vertices on a circuit or switch-leg wire span (`hintKey` is the link id or `"switch:<leg>"`). 1 point draws a smooth arc, 2+ points draw a Catmull-Rom spline, and `null` resets to automatic routing.
- [`documents.setHomeRun`](#documentssethomerun): Aims, resizes, curves, re-attaches, or moves the label of a circuit's home run arrow using offsets relative to its host device so the home run still follows when the device moves.
- [`documents.keynote`](#documentskeynote): Gives elements a keynote by its key ("P1", "M3"); a keynote tag on a view prints the key and the sheet's keynote list (Sheets › Live table › Keynote list) gives its words from the keynote tables in force.
- [`documents.scheduleRows`](#documentsschedulerows): A schedule's rows as numbers and words, on the model as the script has it so far: cells by column id (quantities in SI), grand totals, the row count.
- [`documents.scheduleFields`](#documentsschedulefields): What a schedule can list and show: every class (no argument), or each named class's fields (path, label, type, unit, how it totals) and relationships for aggregate columns.
- [`documents.autoTag`](#documentsautotag): Tag every untagged element of `categories` (`duct`, `pipe`, `air_terminal`, `equipment`, `fixture`, `part`, `room`, `space`, `opening`) in a view as movable `DrawingItem` tags placed clear of linework and other tags.
- [`documents.autoDimension`](#documentsautodimension): Dimensions runs, walls or grid lines in a plan or section as one edit: each (one dimension along every element) or chain (one string across them).
- [`documents.packSheet`](#documentspacksheet): Arranges a sheet's viewports in its drawing area (the editor's Arrange): packed or a grid, optionally shrinking views to a standard scale that fits, as one edit.
- [`documents.diagramKinds`](#documentsdiagramkinds): Lists every live diagram kind registered by active packs (`"one_line"`, `"electrical_riser"`, `"controls_diagram"`, `"plumbing_riser"`, …) with its label.
- [`documents.diagram`](#documentsdiagram): Creates a live diagram view derived from the model by any active pack (`"one_line"`, `"electrical_riser"`, `"controls_diagram"`, `"plumbing_riser"`, …; `documents.diagramKinds(ctx)` lists all available kinds).
- [`documents.oneLine`](#documentsoneline): A one-line, riser, or pack-contributed live diagram in a new drafting view: drawn from a distribution you describe (diagram), or live from the model (live: "one_line", "electrical_riser", "controls_diagram", "plumbing_riser"…).
- [`documents.detailLibrary`](#documentsdetaillibrary): The 2D detail library: components (id, name, category, default size in mm, whether it stretches), hatch and line patterns, line styles and weights.
- [`documents.formKinds`](#documentsformkinds): The form schedule kinds the model's add-ons offer (panel, switchboard, feeder, connection_types, equipment_connections, lighting_controls…) and whether each is the schedule of one element.
- [`documents.formSchedule`](#documentsformschedule): A form schedule view (panel, switchboard, feeder, lighting_controls…) with the add-on's built-in form, filled live from the model; rules (a load read's rules.id) prints code demand factors.

## documents.sheet

A new sheet (number, name, title block); returns its id.

```ts
sheet(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { number: string; name: string; titleBlock?: TitleBlock; fields?: Record<string, string>; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: sheet, drawing, title block, sheets

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-101", name: "Mechanical plan, Level 1" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setSheet

Changes a sheet's number, name, title block or fields.

```ts
setSheet(ctx: ScriptContext, sheetId: string, changes: { number: string; name: string; titleBlock?: TitleBlock; fields?: Record<string, string> }): void
```

Topics: sheet, rename, title block fields

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const s = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-101", name: "Mechanical plan" });
    documents.setSheet(ctx, s, { number: "M-101", name: "Mechanical plan, Level 1", fields: { drawn_by: "KE" } });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.planView

A floor plan of one level (for a discipline, scale, detailLevel, symbolScale, showLineCodes, and per-category/service overrides including singleLineBelow); returns the view's id.

```ts
planView(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: PlanViewSpec): string
```

Topics: view, plan, floor plan, detail level, symbolScale, annotative, single line, double line, line code

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plumbing", discipline: "plumbing", scale: 48, detailLevel: "medium" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setView

Changes a view's detail level (coarse/medium/fine), visual style, annotative `symbolScale` (0.5–3.0), inline service codes, scale, discipline, or per-category/service graphics overrides (including singleLineBelow).

```ts
setView(ctx: ScriptContext, viewId: string, changes: ViewChanges): void
```

Topics: view, detail level, symbolScale, annotative, category overrides, single line, double line, schematic, line code

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plumbing", discipline: "plumbing" });
    documents.setView(ctx, plan, { detailLevel: "medium", showLineCodes: true, scale: 48 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.ceilingView

A reflected ceiling plan of one level; returns the view's id.

```ts
ceilingView(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: PlanViewSpec): string
```

Topics: view, ceiling, rcp

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },

  run(ctx) {
    documents.ceilingView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - RCP", scale: 48 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.sectionView

A vertical building section cut from `from` to `to` (direction +1 left / -1 right, depth default 20 ft); supports annotative `headExt`/`tailExt`, Revit `splitGap` break, explicit `crop`, and `levelLeftExtMm`/`levelRightExtMm` datum extensions. Its live section mark prints automatically on overlapping plans. Returns the view's id.

```ts
sectionView(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: VerticalViewSpec): string
```

Topics: view, section, section cut, building section, section marker, split gap, level lines

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const sec = documents.sectionView(ctx, { name: "Building Section A-A", from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(10) }, to: { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(10) }, direction: 1, depth: units.ft(15), scale: 48, splitGap: true });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "A-301", name: "Sections" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, sec, { x: units.mm(400), y: units.mm(300) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.elevationView

An interior or exterior elevation looking from `from..to` (direction +1 left / -1 right, depth default 20 ft); its live elevation marker (circle + pointer arrow with auto-updating detail#/sheet# head) prints automatically on overlapping plans. Returns the view's id.

```ts
elevationView(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: VerticalViewSpec): string
```

Topics: view, elevation, interior elevation, exterior elevation, elevation marker

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const elev = documents.elevationView(ctx, { name: "Restroom North Elevation", from: { x: units.ft(2), y: units.ft(8) }, to: { x: units.ft(12), y: units.ft(8) }, direction: 1, depth: units.ft(10), scale: 24 });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "A-401", name: "Interior Elevations" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, elev, { x: units.mm(400), y: units.mm(300) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.enlargedPlan

A Revit-style enlarged plan in one step: creates a cropped plan view on the same level at enlarged scale (default 1/4" or 1/2" = 1'-0") AND places a live parametric callout bubble on the parent plan whose detail#/sheet# head auto-updates when the enlarged plan moves sheets. Returns `{ viewId, calloutId }`.

```ts
enlargedPlan(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: EnlargedPlanSpec): { viewId: string; calloutId: string }
```

Topics: view, enlarged plan, callout, callout bubble, plan callout, detail callout

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    const { viewId } = documents.enlargedPlan(ctx, { parent: plan, name: "Enlarged Restroom Plan", from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(12), y: units.ft(10) }, scale: 24 });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "P-401", name: "Enlarged Plumbing Plans" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, viewId, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(300) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.callout

Places a live parametric callout box + split head bubble on a view referencing any existing enlarged plan, 2D detail, section, or elevation view. The head reads the target's live detail#/sheet# automatically; returns the callout's id.

```ts
callout(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: CalloutRefSpec): string
```

Topics: callout, callout bubble, view reference, enlarged plan, detail reference

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    const detail = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Enlarged Core", scale: 24, crop: { from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(10) } } });
    documents.callout(ctx, { view: plan, target: detail, from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(10) }, label: "EEP" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setCrop

Sets a view's crop box in typed units, toggles cropView/showCropBox, or adjusts section/elevation far clip depth, level datum extensions (`levelLeftExtMm`/`levelRightExtMm`), and section mark `headExt`/`tailExt`/`splitGap`.

```ts
setCrop(ctx: ScriptContext, view: string, spec: CropBoxSpec): void
```

Topics: crop, crop box, view crop, enlarged plan, far clip, section marker, level lines

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    documents.setCrop(ctx, plan, { from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(12) } });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.duplicateView

A copy of a view (another discipline's plan of the same level); returns the new id.

```ts
duplicateView(ctx: ScriptContext, viewId: string, name: string, id?: string): string
```

Topics: view, copy, duplicate

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

