```ts
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const m = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Mechanical", discipline: "mechanical" });
    documents.duplicateView(ctx, m, "Level 1 - Plumbing");
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.place

Puts a view (a plan, a schedule, a detail) on a sheet at a point (its centre, from the sheet's lower-left corner), with optional scale and viewport title offset/rule length; returns the viewport's id.

```ts
place(ctx: ScriptContext, sheetId: string, viewId: string, at: SheetPoint, scale?: number, title?: { offset?: { x: Measure; y: Measure }; ruleLength?: Measure }): string
```

Topics: viewport, place, sheet, layout, view title

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const s = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-101", name: "Mechanical plan" });
    const v = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "L1 Mechanical" });
    documents.place(ctx, s, v, { x: units.mm(420), y: units.mm(300) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setViewportTitle

Moves a placed viewport's title block on its sheet (`offset`) and/or changes the horizontal title underline length (`ruleLength`, or `null` to reset).

```ts
setViewportTitle(ctx: ScriptContext, viewportId: string, spec: { offset?: { x: Measure; y: Measure }; ruleLength?: Measure | null }): void
```

Topics: viewport, view title, title line, sheet, layout

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const s = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "A-101", name: "Floor Plan" });
    const v = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "L1 Plan" });
    const vp = documents.place(ctx, s, v, { x: units.mm(420), y: units.mm(300) });
    documents.setViewportTitle(ctx, vp, { offset: { x: units.mm(0), y: units.mm(12) }, ruleLength: units.mm(95) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.editSchedule

Edits a list schedule view in one undo step: add, move, remove or rename columns, filter, sort, group, totals (an equipment schedule's sort, a fixture schedule's DFU total). The same steps the grid's Columns menu and the agent's bim_schedule_define send; a form schedule (panel slots) refuses.

```ts
editSchedule(ctx: ScriptContext, viewId: string, steps: ScheduleEditStep[]): void
```

Topics: schedule, columns, rename column, sort, filter, group, totals

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { ids: ["sched-equipment"] },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    documents.editSchedule(ctx, "sched-equipment", [{ op: "rename_column", columnId: "mark", heading: "TAG" }, { op: "sort", sort: [{ path: "mark", direction: "asc" }] }, { op: "totals", show: true }]);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.schedule

A schedule view; returns its id. Give classes (rooms, spaces, zones, equipment, any class documents.scheduleFields lists) with field paths or full columns, filters, sort, groups and totals; or a category for a one-category list. Put it on a sheet with documents.place; change it later with documents.editSchedule.

```ts
schedule(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { name: string; category: ScheduleCategory; columns: readonly string[]; title?: string; id?: string } | { name: string; classes: readonly string[]; columns: readonly (string | ScheduleColumn)[]; levels?: readonly string[]; filters?: readonly ScheduleFilter[]; sort?: readonly (string | { path: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" })[]; groups?: readonly (string | { path: string; header?: boolean; footer?: boolean; totals?: boolean })[]; totals?: boolean; includeSubclasses?: boolean; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: schedule, make a schedule, room schedule, space schedule, equipment schedule, table, classes

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: units.ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }], thickness: units.in(4), height: units.ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const rooms = documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Room schedule", classes: ["arch.room"], columns: ["number", "name", "area"], sort: ["number"], totals: true });
    const equipmentSchedule = documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Equipment schedule", category: "mechanical_equipment", columns: ["mark", "type_name", "level"] });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "A-601", name: "Schedules" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, rooms, { x: units.mm(150), y: units.mm(400) });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, equipmentSchedule, { x: units.mm(450), y: units.mm(400) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.tag

A tag on one element in a plan view (its mark, size or the right text for its kind), with a leader; returns the tag's id.

```ts
tag(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { view: string; element: string; at: { x: Measure; y: Measure }; template?: TagTemplate; fields?: readonly string[]; leader?: boolean; leaderOverride?: boolean; elbow?: "auto" | { x: Measure; y: Measure }; mask?: boolean; textSizeMm?: number; styleId?: string; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: tag, tags, label, mark, annotate

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    documents.tag(ctx, { view: plan, element: walls.element(1), at: { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(-3) } });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.moveTag

Moves an existing tag in a plan view to a clear position (and optionally toggles its leader).

```ts
moveTag(ctx: ScriptContext, tagId: string, at: { x: Measure; y: Measure }, opts?: { leader?: boolean }): void
```

Topics: move tag, tag, label, overlap, legibility

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    const t = documents.tag(ctx, { view: plan, element: walls.element(1), at: { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(-3) } });
    documents.moveTag(ctx, t, { x: units.ft(12), y: units.ft(-4) }, { leader: true });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.planLabels

Returns every rendered text label on a plan view (paper mm coordinates and bounding boxes) plus any overlapping pairs, so scripts can verify legibility and move colliding tags.

```ts
planLabels(ctx: ScriptContext, viewRef: string): { viewId: string; scale: number; labels: { text: string; at: { xMm: number; yMm: number }; sizeMm: number; anchor: string; box: { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number } }[]; overlaps: { a: string; b: string; overlapAreaMm2: number }[] }
```

Topics: plan labels, overlaps, legibility, tags, inspect, qa

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    const report = documents.planLabels(ctx, plan);
    ctx.label(`${report.labels.length} labels, ${report.overlaps.length} overlaps`);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.dimension

A dimension between two points in a view, tied to elements with refs so it follows them; returns its id.

```ts
dimension(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { view: string; from: PlanPoint; to: PlanPoint; refs?: ({ elementId: string; anchor: string } | null)[]; offset?: Measure; kind?: "linear" | "aligned"; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: dimension, dimensions, measure, annotate

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    documents.dimension(ctx, { view: plan, from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, refs: [{ elementId: walls.element(1), anchor: "start" }, { elementId: walls.element(1), anchor: "end" }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.tagStyle

A new tag style: field lines, box, orientation, what it applies to, and an arrow along the run (`arrow: "down_slope"` points downhill on the view's paper, `"up_slope"` uphill; level pipe shows none); returns its id.

```ts
tagStyle(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: Omit<Extract<EditCommand, { type: "create_tag_style" }>, "type" | "styleId"> & { id?: string }): string
```

Topics: tag style, slope arrow, downhill arrow, drain slope tag, tag, arrow

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts

  kind: "layout",
  reads: {},
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    documents.tagStyle(ctx, { name: "Drain slope", lines: ["[{pipe.slope}]"], box: "none", orientation: "along", appliesTo: ["pipe"], arrow: "down_slope" });
  },
});
```

</details>

Changes a tag style's look: lines, box, orientation, applies-to, mask, textStyleId or its arrow (`arrow: "none"` removes it).

```ts
setTagStyle(ctx: ScriptContext, styleId: string, changes: Omit<Extract<EditCommand, { type: "update_tag_style" }>, "type" | "styleId">): void
```

</details>

## documents.textStyle

Creates a model-wide Text Type (font family, paper cap height, bold/italic/uppercase, opaque or transparent background mask, default drawing roles) so part marks, circuit labels, tags, dimensions and room labels stay unified and readable over crossing lines.

```ts
textStyle(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { name: string; textSizeMm?: number; fontFamily?: string; bold?: boolean; italic?: boolean; uppercase?: boolean; background?: "opaque" | "transparent"; color?: string; defaultFor?: readonly TextStyleRole[]; id?: string }): string
```

```ts
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setCircuitGraphics

Sets a plan view's circuit and switch-leg drawing style (`showCircuits: false` makes a dedicated controls schematic plan), home runs, switch-leg letters, and ANSI/NECA 100 wire hash marks (`home_runs`, `home_runs_and_switch_legs`, or `all_runs`) while keeping existing wire waypoints and home-run offsets intact.

```ts
setCircuitGraphics(ctx: ScriptContext, viewRef: string, settings: CircuitGraphicsSettingsSpec): void
```

Topics: circuit graphics, wire style, hash marks, tick marks, switch legs, home runs, controls plan

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts

  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    documents.setCircuitGraphics(ctx, plan, { style: "arcs", showCircuits: true, homeRuns: true, switchLegs: true, switchLegLabels: true, hashMarks: "hots_neutral_ground", hashMarksOn: "home_runs_and_switch_legs" });
  },
});
```

</details>

Groups (or splits with `null`) branch circuits on the same panel into a shared-neutral Multi-Wire Branch Circuit (MWBC, NEC 210.4) drawn as one multi-arrowhead combined home run with shared neutral hash marks.

```ts
setMwbcGroup(ctx: ScriptContext, viewRef: string, linkIds: readonly string[], groupName: string | null): void
```

## documents.setWirePath

Pins one or more spline/orthogonal control vertices on a circuit or switch-leg wire span (`hintKey` is the link id or `"switch:<leg>"`). 1 point draws a smooth arc, 2+ points draw a Catmull-Rom spline, and `null` resets to automatic routing.

```ts
setWirePath(ctx: ScriptContext, viewRef: string, hintKey: string, fromElementId: string, toElementId: string, waypoints: readonly PlanPoint[] | null): void
```

Topics: spline wire, wire vertices, wire path, bend circuit, arc wire

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    documents.setWirePath(ctx, plan, "ckt-1", "r-1", "r-2", [{ x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(12) }, { x: units.ft(16), y: units.ft(13) }]);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setHomeRun

Aims, resizes, curves, re-attaches, or moves the label of a circuit's home run arrow using offsets relative to its host device so the home run still follows when the device moves. Pass `null` to reset.

```ts
setHomeRun(ctx: ScriptContext, viewRef: string, linkId: string, spec: HomeRunSpec | null): void
```

Topics: home run, move home run, home run arrow, circuit label, home run curve

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    documents.setHomeRun(ctx, plan, "ckt-1", { tipOffset: { x: units.ft(-4), y: units.ft(-1.5) }, bendOffset: { x: units.ft(-2), y: units.ft(-2) } });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.keynote

Gives elements a keynote by its key ("P1", "M3"); a keynote tag on a view prints the key and the sheet's keynote list (Sheets › Live table › Keynote list) gives its words from the keynote tables in force.

```ts
keynote(ctx: ScriptContext, elementIds: readonly string[], key: string): void
```

```ts
  },

```

</details>

## documents.scheduleRows

A schedule's rows as numbers and words, on the model as the script has it so far: cells by column id (quantities in SI), grand totals, the row count. Form schedules (panels, feeders) are add-on reads (electrical.loads).

```ts
scheduleRows(ctx: ScriptContext, schedule: string, window?: { offset?: number; limit?: number }): ScheduleRows
```

Topics: schedule rows, read a schedule, totals, room areas, schedule values

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: units.ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }], thickness: units.in(4), height: units.ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const rooms = documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Room schedule", classes: ["arch.room"], columns: ["number", "name", "area"], sort: ["number"], totals: true });
    const read = documents.scheduleRows(ctx, rooms);
    const m2 = read.rows.reduce((sum, r) => sum + Number(r.cells.area ?? 0), 0);
    ctx.label(`${read.totalRows} rooms, ${Math.round(m2 * 10.7639)} sq ft`);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.scheduleFields

What a schedule can list and show: every class (no argument), or each named class's fields (path, label, type, unit, how it totals) and relationships for aggregate columns.

```ts
scheduleFields(ctx: ScriptContext, classes?: readonly string[]): readonly ScheduleClassFields[]
```

Topics: schedule fields, schedule classes, what can a schedule show, columns

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const space = documents.scheduleFields(ctx, ["gen.space"])[0];
    const fields = (space?.fields ?? []).filter((f) => f.path === "area" || f.path === "occupants").map((f) => f.path);
    documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Space schedule", classes: ["gen.space"], columns: ["number", "name", ...fields], totals: true });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.autoTag

Tag every untagged element of `categories` (`duct`, `pipe`, `air_terminal`, `equipment`, `fixture`, `part`, `room`, `space`, `opening`) in a view as movable `DrawingItem` tags placed clear of linework and other tags.

```ts
autoTag(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { view: string; categories: readonly AutoTagCategory[]; leaders?: "always" | "never" | "when_away"; includeTagged?: boolean; only?: readonly string[]; textHeight?: Measure; styleId?: string }): { tagged: number; skipped: readonly { elementId: string; reason: string }[] }
```

Topics: auto tag, tag all, tag every duct, tags, annotate

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Mechanical", scale: 48, cutHeight: units.ft(10) });
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(20), units.in(12)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(2), y: units.ft(10) }, { x: units.ft(28), y: units.ft(10) }] });
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(20), units.in(12)), system: { id: "ra-1", kind: "return_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(2) }, { x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(18) }] });
    const done = documents.autoTag(ctx, { view: plan, categories: ["duct"] });
    ctx.label(`${done.tagged} duct tags`);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.autoDimension

Dimensions runs, walls or grid lines in a plan or section as one edit: each (one dimension along every element) or chain (one string across them). Every dimension follows its elements.

```ts
autoDimension(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { view: string; elements: readonly string[]; mode: "each" | "chain"; direction?: "horizontal" | "vertical"; offset?: Measure }): void
```

Topics: auto dimension, dimension walls, dimension string, chain dimension, dimensions

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    documents.autoDimension(ctx, { view: plan, elements: [walls.element(1), walls.element(2)], mode: "each" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.packSheet

Arranges a sheet's viewports in its drawing area (the editor's Arrange): packed or a grid, optionally shrinking views to a standard scale that fits, as one edit. Returns how many moved.

```ts
packSheet(ctx: ScriptContext, sheet: string, spec?: { mode?: "pack" | "grid"; columns?: number; fitScales?: boolean; minScale?: number; order?: readonly string[]; gap?: Measure }): { moved: number }
```

Topics: sheet layout, arrange sheet, pack views, sheet packing, fit views

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-101", name: "Plans" });
    for (const level of ctx.model.levels()) {
      const view = documents.planView(ctx, { level: level.id, name: `${String(level.name)} - Mechanical`, scale: 48 });
      documents.place(ctx, sheet, view, { x: units.mm(100), y: units.mm(100) });
    }
    documents.packSheet(ctx, sheet, { fitScales: true });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.diagramKinds

Lists every live diagram kind registered by active packs (`"one_line"`, `"electrical_riser"`, `"controls_diagram"`, `"plumbing_riser"`, …) with its label.

```ts
diagramKinds(ctx: ScriptContext): readonly { kind: string; label: string }[]
```

Topics: diagram kinds, controls diagram, one-line, riser diagram, live diagram

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.label(documents.diagramKinds(ctx).map((d) => d.kind).join(", "));
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.diagram

Creates a live diagram view derived from the model by any active pack (`"one_line"`, `"electrical_riser"`, `"controls_diagram"`, `"plumbing_riser"`, …; `documents.diagramKinds(ctx)` lists all available kinds). Returns the view's id.

```ts
diagram(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { name: string; kind: string; hints?: DiagramHints; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: diagram, live diagram, controls diagram, lighting controls diagram, one-line, riser

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const ctrl = documents.diagram(ctx, { name: "E-501 Lighting Controls Diagram", kind: "controls_diagram" });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "E-501", name: "Electrical Diagrams" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, ctrl, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(300) }, 1);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.oneLine

A one-line, riser, or pack-contributed live diagram in a new drafting view: drawn from a distribution you describe (diagram), or live from the model (live: "one_line", "electrical_riser", "controls_diagram", "plumbing_riser"…). Returns the view's id.

```ts
oneLine(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { name: string; diagram: { title?: string; roots: readonly OneLineNode[]; notes?: readonly string[] }; id?: string } | { name: string; live: string; hints?: Record<string, unknown>; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: one-line, single line, riser diagram, electrical diagram, distribution diagram, controls diagram

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const diagram = documents.oneLine(ctx, { name: "E-601 One-line", diagram: { roots: [{ id: "utility", kind: "utility", name: "Utility", children: [{ id: "msb", kind: "switchboard", name: "MSB", ratings: ["800A", "208Y/120V"], children: [{ id: "lp1", kind: "panelboard", name: "LP-1" }] }] }] } });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "E-601", name: "One-line diagram" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, diagram, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(300) }, 1);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.detailLibrary

The 2D detail library: components (id, name, category, default size in mm, whether it stretches), hatch and line patterns, line styles and weights. Use a component id as the symbol of a detail item.

```ts
detailLibrary(ctx: ScriptContext): { components: readonly { id: string; name: string; category: string; widthMm: number; heightMm: number; linear: boolean }[]; hatchPatterns: readonly string[]; linePatterns: readonly string[]; lineStyles: readonly { id: string; name: string }[]; lineWeights: readonly string[] }
```

Topics: detail components, detail library, hatch patterns, line styles, symbols

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const library = documents.detailLibrary(ctx);
    ctx.label(`${library.components.length} detail components`);
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.formKinds

The form schedule kinds the model's add-ons offer (panel, switchboard, feeder, connection_types, equipment_connections, lighting_controls…) and whether each is the schedule of one element.

```ts
formKinds(ctx: ScriptContext): readonly { kind: string; boundToElement: boolean }[]
```

Topics: form schedule, panel schedule, switchboard schedule, feeder schedule, lighting controls schedule

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.label(documents.formKinds(ctx).map((f) => f.kind).join(", "));
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.formSchedule

A form schedule view (panel, switchboard, feeder, lighting_controls…) with the add-on's built-in form, filled live from the model; rules (a load read's rules.id) prints code demand factors. Returns its id; put it on a sheet with documents.place.

```ts
formSchedule(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { kind: string; name: string; element?: string; rules?: string; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: panel schedule, form schedule, switchboard schedule, lighting controls schedule, controls schedule, schedule a panel

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true, kinds: ["part"] },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: "builtin:panelboard-125-208-1ph@1", at: { x: units.ft(1), y: units.ft(13) }, mark: "LP-1" });
    const panel = ctx.model.ofKind("part").find((p) => p.mark === "LP-1");
    if (!panel) throw new Error("No LP-1");
    const loads = ctx.read<{ rules: { id: string } }>("electrical.loads", { panel: "LP-1", nec_edition: "2023" });
    const schedule = documents.formSchedule(ctx, { kind: "panel", name: "Panel LP-1 schedule", element: panel.id, rules: loads.rules.id });
    const controls = documents.formSchedule(ctx, { kind: "lighting_controls", name: "Lighting controls schedule" });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "E-601", name: "Panel & control schedules" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, schedule, { x: units.mm(250), y: units.mm(350) });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, controls, { x: units.mm(620), y: units.mm(350) });
  },
});
```

</details>

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/checks.md -->

# checks

Checks a script runs on its own output before a person sees it.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`checks.clashes`](#checksclashes): The coordination check on the model as the script has it so far (hard and soft clashes, clearances; or the default, documents or issue rule set), worst first, each with its rule, elements, place and words.

## checks.clashes

The coordination check on the model as the script has it so far (hard and soft clashes, clearances; or the default, documents or issue rule set), worst first, each with its rule, elements, place and words. Read only: move things with ctx.edit.

```ts
clashes(ctx: ScriptContext, spec?: { ruleset?: "default" | "coordination" | "documents" | "issue"; level?: string; ids?: readonly string[]; tolerance?: Measure; skipRules?: readonly string[] }): readonly Finding[]
```

Topics: clash, clash check, coordination, lint, interference, clearance

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Mechanical", scale: 48, cutHeight: units.ft(10) });
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(20), units.in(12)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(2), y: units.ft(10) }, { x: units.ft(28), y: units.ft(10) }] });
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(20), units.in(12)), system: { id: "ra-1", kind: "return_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(2) }, { x: units.ft(15), y: units.ft(18) }] });
    const found = checks.clashes(ctx);
    ctx.label(found.length > 0 ? `Ducts routed; ${found.length} clash to resolve: ${found[0]?.message ?? ""}` : "Ducts routed, no clashes");
  },
});
```

</details>

---

<!-- docs/reference/script-kit/define-script.md -->

# defineScript

The one top-level function: a script's kind, what it reads, its parameters and its `run`.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`defineScript`](#definescript): A script: its kind (part, layout or route), what it reads, its typed parameters and its run.

## defineScript

A script: its kind (part, layout or route), what it reads, its typed parameters and its run. The default export of every script.

```ts
function defineScript<P extends Record<string, ParameterDecl>>(spec: { kind: "part" | "layout" | "route"; reads: ScriptReads; parameters: P; presets?: { id: string; label: string; values: Record<string, string | number | boolean> }[]; run(ctx: ScriptContext, values: ValuesOf<P>): void | Promise<void> }): ScriptDefinition
```

Topics: script, start, parameters, reads, how to write

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.label("One new level");
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

<!-- docs/reference/recipes.md -->

# Script recipes

Worked tasks: which kit functions to call, in which order. Start from the closest one.

## Part definition

Task: parts

The part-type definition a part script returns (what PartBuilder.build() makes and bim_save_part_type saves); never write one by hand, build it.

1. { familyName, typeName, category, description?, typeParams: [{ name, label, kind: length|number|text|boolean|choice, unit? }], typeValues: { name: value (lengths in mm) }, instanceParams: [], connectors: [...], geometry: [], symbol: [], tagFields: ["mark", "type_name"], source: { kind: "script", key?, version? }, model?, clearances? }.
2. connectors[]: { id, label, domain (duct | pipe | electrical | …), systemKind, position: [x, y, z] mm, direction: [x, y, z] out of the part, shape: rect | round | none, width/height or diameter, flowDirection?, endType?, voltage?, poles? }.
3. model (solid program, schema 2): { schema: 2, id, referencePlanes, sketches (points, lines, arcs, circles, fixed by constraints), profiles ({ sketch, outer: { edges }, holes? }), features (extrude | revolve | sweep | loft | imported | pattern | mirror, each join | cut | intersect, visibility per detail level), symbols (per view and detail level), planDisplay, types }.
4. source.kind is "script" for every part a script makes; bim_save_part_type fills key and version with the saved script version.

Uses: `parts.part`, `PartBuilder.build`, `PartBuilder.draft`

## Rooftop unit

Task: equipment

Make an RTU part type, save it, then place it on the roof and duct it.

1. Part script (start from the starter.rooftop_unit library script): extrude the curb (a rectangle with a hole), the casing on it, cut the section seams and access-panel recesses, extrude handles and pattern them, pattern the condenser fan guards on top, a louvred outside-air hood; connectorAt / connector for supply and return (duct, rect, bottom), outside air, gas, power (shape none) and the condensate drain; data fields (weight, curb size) as param(); clearance for service; symbol("coarse") for the plan. ctx.parts.define per size. Preview (the pictures are drawn from the solid), then bim_save_part_type.
2. Layout script: equipment.place on the roof level with the saved type id and onSlab; routes.along from placed.connector("supply") and ("return") down into the building.

Uses: `parts.part`, `PartBuilder.extrude`, `PartBuilder.cut`, `PartBuilder.pattern`, `PartBuilder.connectorAt`, `PartBuilder.symbol`, `ctx.parts.define`, `equipment.place`, `routes.along`

## Water heater

Task: equipment

A tank water heater with cold, hot and gas connectors, placed and piped.

1. Part script (starter.water_heater): a revolved jacket with domed head, a drain valve and a relief valve; connectors on top for cold and hot water (pipe), gas or power by fuel, a flue (duct, round) and the T&P discharge. Save it.
2. Layout script: equipment.place, then routes.along from each connector to the mains (routes.atRunEnd or a branch).

Uses: `parts.part`, `PartBuilder.revolve`, `PartBuilder.cylinder`, `PartBuilder.connector`, `equipment.place`, `routes.along`, `routes.branch`

## Electrical panel and panel schedule

Task: electrical

A panelboard, receptacles by code spacing, circuits from a room template, and the panel's loads per phase, in one script.

1. equipment.place a starter panelboard (parts.starterTypes(ctx, "panelboard") lists them).
2. ctx.propose("electrical.receptacles") on the rooms, then ctx.acceptGhosts.
3. Save a room template (save_catalog_entry, type circuit_template); ctx.read("electrical.circuit_template_plan") plans the circuits for whole rooms and ctx.editSteps sends them.
4. One circuit by hand: each circuit is a service link from the panel to the devices it feeds, sent with ctx.edit({ type: "create_service_link", sourceId: panel.id, positions: [1], members: [{ elementId, connector: "power" }], electrical: { ratingA: 20 } }) (bim_script_reference({ command: "create_service_link" }) lists its fields).
5. ctx.read("electrical.loads") for connected and demand loads per phase; "electrical.rebalance_plan" to even the phases; "electrical.check" for overloads and unbalance. A panel schedule is a form: make it with documents.formSchedule and documents.place it on an E sheet. documents.editSchedule refuses a form; use it on list schedules such as the lighting fixture schedule.

Uses: `equipment.place`, `ctx.propose`, `ctx.acceptGhosts`, `ctx.read`, `ctx.editSteps`, `documents.place`

## Drains with slope

Task: pipe routing

Sanitary or storm piping that falls along its run, or many fixtures connected into a main at once.

1. One route script: routes.along with slope { rise, per } (absent: the system's minimum); routes.connectInto for many fixtures at once.

Uses: `routes.along`, `routes.connectInto`, `routes.pipe`

## Walls, doors and windows

Task: walls

A building outline with openings and rooms in one layout script.

1. building.walls closed, building.door / building.window on walls.element(n), building.floor, building.space per room.

Uses: `building.walls`, `building.door`, `building.window`, `building.floor`, `building.space`

## Sheets per level

Task: sheets

One sheet per level with its plan, schedules on a schedule sheet, numbered in print order; a person picks the sheets when printing and issuing.

1. ctx.model.levels(); per level documents.sheet (numbered in print order: M-101, M-102) + documents.planView + documents.place.

Uses: `ctx.model`, `documents.sheet`, `documents.planView`, `documents.place`

## One script for many steps

Task: many edits

Prefer one script over many single tool calls: a layout of dozens of edits is one preview, one Approve and one Undo.

1. Read what you need once (reads), loop in the script, ctx.label the result; preview with bim_run_script.

Uses: `defineScript`, `ctx.model`, `ctx.edit`, `ctx.label`

## Schedules

Task: schedules

A schedule of one category's elements with chosen columns, placed on a schedule sheet.

1. documents.schedule with the category and columns; documents.place it on a sheet; later changes (sort, totals, renamed columns) with documents.editSchedule.

Uses: `documents.schedule`, `documents.sheet`, `documents.place`, `documents.editSchedule`

## Rooms from walls

Task: rooms and spaces

Rooms found from the walls that enclose them, one point inside each room.

1. building.walls (closed, or meeting other walls), then building.spaceInWalls with a point inside each room; an open room is refused in words.

Uses: `building.walls`, `building.spaceInWalls`, `building.space`

## Levels

Task: levels

New levels at elevations, or one above the highest level the model has.

1. ctx.model.levels() to read what exists; building.level for each new one.

Uses: `ctx.model`, `building.level`

## Duct routing

Task: duct routing

A supply main with a branch, sized from a duct friction calculation.

1. ctx.calc mech.duct_friction to check a size; routes.along for the main; routes.branch off it; routes.drop for a riser.

Uses: `ctx.calc`, `routes.along`, `routes.branch`, `routes.rect`, `routes.round`

## Pipe routing

Task: pipe routing

A drain sized by the plumbing code, then routed with its slope.

1. ctx.calc plumbing.size_drain (name the edition); routes.along with routes.pipe at that size and the slope; routes.connectInto for many fixtures at once.

Uses: `ctx.calc`, `routes.along`, `routes.pipe`, `routes.connectInto`

## Tags

Task: tags

Tags on elements in a plan view.

1. A plan view (documents.planView, or one the model has); documents.autoTag tags every duct, pipe, terminal or fixture clear of the others; documents.tag places one where you say.

Uses: `documents.planView`, `documents.autoTag`, `documents.tag`

## Dimensions

Task: dimensions

A dimension tied to the elements it measures, so it follows them when they move.

1. A plan view; documents.autoDimension for every run, wall or grid line (each, or one chain); documents.dimension for one between two points, with refs to the elements' ends.

Uses: `documents.planView`, `documents.autoDimension`, `documents.dimension`

## Checks and lint

Task: lint and checks

Find what is wrong with bim_validation_issues (a core read), then fix it in one script; a calculation can check a design before it is drawn.

1. bim_validation_issues lists the model's own checks (an open end, a missing size, a slope below the minimum).
2. One script fixes them (ctx.edit with the command that corrects each); ctx.calc checks a size or a slope before the script draws it.
3. checks.clashes runs the coordination check (clashes, clearances) on the model as the script has it, so a script can route, check and move in one run.
4. Accepting a coordination finding and lint settings are kept by the host app: not a script's job.

Uses: `ctx.calc`, `checks.clashes`, `ctx.edit`, `ctx.model`

## Imports

Task: imports

A plan PDF or image placed under a level to trace over; bringing in an outside model is a host step.

1. ctx.edit place_underlay with a file the host app stores (its provider and ref), then calibrate_underlay, then trace walls or spaces over it.
2. Linking or importing an outside model (IFC, another company's cloud) goes through the host app, and the agent asks the person; a script then reads and edits around the linked reference.

Uses: `ctx.edit`

## Calculations

Task: calculations

Run an engineering calculation from a script and act on the answer.

1. ctx.calcs() lists them; ctx.calc runs one on the model the script has (name the code edition); read run.values by key and use them in edits; ctx.label says what was decided.

Uses: `ctx.calcs`, `ctx.calc`, `ctx.label`

## Receptacles by code spacing

Task: receptacles

Receptacles in rooms by NEC 210.52 wall spacing (or a density preset), each with its clause, placed as one edit.

1. Rooms (building.room, or the model's); ctx.propose("electrical.receptacles", { typeId, roomIds, options: { mode: "dwelling", edition } }); read proposal.summary (passes or not); ctx.acceptGhosts with the ghosts to keep. Circuiting is a separate step.

Uses: `building.room`, `ctx.propose`, `ctx.acceptGhosts`

## Room and space schedules

Task: room schedules

A schedule of rooms, spaces or zones (any class) with fields, totals, sorting and grouping, on a sheet.

1. documents.scheduleFields(ctx, ["gen.space"]) lists the fields; documents.schedule with classes and columns (totals: true adds the grand total); documents.place it on a sheet.

Uses: `documents.scheduleFields`, `documents.schedule`, `documents.place`

## Read a schedule's numbers

Task: schedule values

A schedule's rows and totals as numbers, to decide edits (sizes, counts, what is missing).

1. documents.scheduleRows(ctx, schedule) on any list schedule: cells by column id (SI), totals, row count. Panel and feeder forms: ctx.read("electrical.loads").

Uses: `documents.scheduleRows`

## Rebalance a panel

Task: panel rebalancing

Move circuits between slots so the panel's phases carry even loads, as one edit.

1. ctx.read("electrical.rebalance_plan", { panel }) returns the moves, before and after VA per phase, and the command (null when nothing helps); ctx.editSteps(plan.command) sends it.

Uses: `ctx.read`, `ctx.editSteps`

## Room circuit templates

Task: circuit templates

A firm's room convention (bedroom on one circuit, living room on another) applied to dwelling units on the panels you name.

1. Save the template (save_catalog_entry, type circuit_template) or use the model's; ctx.read("electrical.circuit_template_plan", { template, units: [{ panel, rooms }] }); ctx.editSteps(plan.command). The script names each unit's panel: nothing picks one.

Uses: `ctx.edit`, `ctx.read`, `ctx.editSteps`

## Tag and dimension a plan

Task: annotate a plan

Every duct tagged clear of the others and the walls dimensioned, in one script.

1. documents.autoTag(ctx, { view, categories }) then documents.autoDimension(ctx, { view, elements, mode }).

Uses: `documents.autoTag`, `documents.autoDimension`

## Pack sheets

Task: sheet layout

Views placed on a sheet and arranged to fit its drawing area.

1. documents.place each view (anywhere), then documents.packSheet(ctx, sheet, { mode, fitScales }).

Uses: `documents.place`, `documents.packSheet`

## One-line diagram

Task: one-line

An electrical one-line drawn from a distribution you describe, or a live one-line or riser from the model, on a sheet.

1. documents.oneLine(ctx, { name, diagram }) or { name, live: "one_line" }; documents.place it at scale 1.

Uses: `documents.oneLine`, `documents.place`

## Size ducts from airflow

Task: duct sizing

The duct size a system's friction, velocity and aspect limits call for, used to route or resize.

1. ctx.read("mechanical.duct_size", { cfm, shape, height_mm }) or { element_id } for a routed segment; route or resize with the suggested size (mm).

Uses: `ctx.read`, `routes.along`

## Clash check

Task: coordination

Route, check for clashes and adjust in one script.

1. checks.clashes(ctx) after the routes: each finding names the elements and where; move one with ctx.edit (or route it at another height) and check again.

Uses: `checks.clashes`, `routes.along`

## Levels from a linked model

Task: linked levels

The model's levels matched to a linked architectural model's storeys.

1. Give the storeys (the host's link lists them; a script takes them as values); building.levelSyncPlan previews; building.syncLevels applies.

Uses: `building.levelSyncPlan`, `building.syncLevels`

## Catalogues

Task: catalogues

What the libraries hold: starter part types, fitting families, detail components, and the electrical and plumbing catalogues.

1. parts.starterTypes, routes.fittingTypes, documents.detailLibrary; ctx.read("electrical.catalog") and ctx.read("bim_plumbing_catalog") for the add-ons'. The firm's saved library is the host's.

Uses: `parts.starterTypes`, `routes.fittingTypes`, `documents.detailLibrary`, `ctx.read`

## Ceiling and floor heights

Task: surfaces

The floor, ceiling, roof and structure over a point, to set a run's or a unit's height.

1. building.surfacesAt(ctx, { at, level }) or { element }; use ceiling or structureAbove elevationMm to pick a height.

Uses: `building.surfacesAt`, `routes.along`

---

<!-- docs/reference/examples.md -->

# Example scripts

Whole scripts that each build something complete. Copy the closest one and change it.

## Small office

Two floors of a 40 x 30 ft office: exterior and interior walls, doors and windows, rooms found from the walls (open office, conference, office), and a plan of each floor on its own sheet.

Run it: `npm run example -- small-office`, or paste it to an assistant connected to the tool server. Source: [`packages/bim-script/examples/small-office.ts`](../../packages/bim-script/examples/small-office.ts).

```ts
/**
 * Small office: two floors of a 40 ft x 30 ft office.
 *
 * Each floor gets exterior walls, interior walls that split it into an open
 * office, a conference room and a private office, doors and windows, and
 * rooms found from the walls around them (nobody draws a room outline), and
 * a ceiling in each room. Then each floor gets a plan on its own sheet.
 *
 * Level arguments are level ids: building.level returns the id every call
 * below passes as `level`. On a model that already has levels, read them
 * (reads.levels: true) and pass an id from ctx.model.levels(); the kit's
 * helpers also take the name of exactly one level ("Level 2").
 *
 * Run it: paste it to an assistant connected to the MutinyBIM tool server
 * ("run this script"), or `npm run example -- small-office`.
 */
import { defineScript, units, building, documents } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

const ft = units.ft;
const at = (x: number, y: number) => ({ x: ft(x), y: ft(y) });

export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.label("Small office: two floors with walls, rooms, ceilings, doors and windows, and a plan sheet per floor");
    const made: { level: string; id: string; rooms: string[] }[] = [];

    const floors = [
      { name: "Level 1", elevation: ft(0), sheet: "A-101" },
      { name: "Level 2", elevation: ft(12), sheet: "A-102" },
    ];

    for (const floor of floors) {
      const level = building.level(ctx, { name: floor.name, elevation: floor.elevation });

      // The outside: four walls, 8 in thick, closed back to the first corner.
      // Wall 1 runs along the south side, wall 3 along the north.
      const outside = building.walls(ctx, { level, points: [at(0, 0), at(40, 0), at(40, 30), at(0, 30)], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: ft(11) });

      // Inside: one wall north to south at 24 ft, and one east of it at 15 ft.
      const split = building.walls(ctx, { level, points: [at(24, 0), at(24, 30)], thickness: units.in(5), height: ft(11) });
      const office = building.walls(ctx, { level, points: [at(24, 15), at(40, 15)], thickness: units.in(5), height: ft(11) });

      // Doors are placed along a wall, from its start. The entry is on the ground floor only.
      if (floor.name === "Level 1") building.door(ctx, { wall: outside.element(1), along: ft(10), width: units.in(36), mark: "101A" });
      building.door(ctx, { wall: split.element(1), along: ft(22), width: units.in(36) });
      building.door(ctx, { wall: office.element(1), along: ft(4), width: units.in(36) });

      // Windows on the north wall (it runs east to west, so 6 ft along it is near the east end).
      for (const along of [6, 18, 30]) building.window(ctx, { wall: outside.element(3), along: ft(along), width: ft(4), height: ft(5) });

      // Rooms from the walls: one point inside each, the kernel traces the enclosure.
      const n = floor.name === "Level 1" ? 100 : 200;
      const open = building.spaceInWalls(ctx, { level, inside: at(10, 15), number: `${n + 1}`, name: "Open office" });
      const conference = building.spaceInWalls(ctx, { level, inside: at(32, 7), number: `${n + 2}`, name: "Conference" });
      const privateOffice = building.spaceInWalls(ctx, { level, inside: at(32, 22), number: `${n + 3}`, name: "Office" });

      // A 9 ft ceiling in each room, its outline 1 ft inside the walls (units.* values, no millimetres by hand).
      const inset = (x0: number, y0: number, x1: number, y1: number) => [at(x0 + 1, y0 + 1), at(x1 - 1, y0 + 1), at(x1 - 1, y1 - 1), at(x0 + 1, y1 - 1)];
      building.ceiling(ctx, { level, space: open, outline: inset(0, 0, 24, 30), height: ft(9) });
      building.ceiling(ctx, { level, space: conference, outline: inset(24, 0, 40, 15), height: ft(9) });
      building.ceiling(ctx, { level, space: privateOffice, outline: inset(24, 15, 40, 30), height: ft(9) });
      made.push({ level: floor.name, id: level, rooms: [open, conference, privateOffice] });

      // A plan of this floor on its own sheet, 1/4" = 1'-0".
      const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: floor.sheet, name: `${floor.name} floor plan` });
      const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level, name: `${floor.name} - Plan`, scale: 48 });
      documents.place(ctx, sheet, plan, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(280) });
    }

    // What the script made, for the agent: it comes back as `report` beside the preview.
    ctx.report("Levels and rooms", made);
  },
});
```

## Rooftop unit

A 10 ton rooftop unit built as a part type, placed on the roof, its supply and return ducts sized from airflow and routed down into two rooms, every duct tagged, and an equipment schedule on a sheet.

Run it: `npm run example -- rooftop-unit`, or paste it to an assistant connected to the tool server. Source: [`packages/bim-script/examples/rooftop-unit.ts`](../../packages/bim-script/examples/rooftop-unit.ts).

```ts
/**
 * Rooftop unit: a 10 ton unit on the roof, ducted down into two rooms.
 *
 * The script sizes the supply and return ducts with the duct sizing read
 * (the system's friction and velocity limits), builds the unit's part type
 * with connectors of that size, places it on the roof, and routes its
 * supply and return down into the rooms. Then it tags the ducts on a plan
 * and puts an equipment schedule on a sheet.
 *
 * Run it: paste it to an assistant connected to the MutinyBIM tool server
 * ("run this script"), or `npm run example -- rooftop-unit`.
 */
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

const ft = units.ft;
const at = (x: number, y: number) => ({ x: ft(x), y: ft(y) });

/** 10 tons at 400 CFM per ton. */
const SUPPLY_CFM = 4000;

export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    // The building: one floor, 60 ft x 30 ft, two rooms side by side, a 10 ft ceiling.
    const level = building.level(ctx, { name: "Level 1", elevation: ft(0) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level, points: [at(0, 0), at(60, 0), at(60, 30), at(0, 30)], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: ft(14) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level, points: [at(30, 0), at(30, 30)], thickness: units.in(5), height: ft(14) });
    building.spaceInWalls(ctx, { level, inside: at(15, 15), number: "101", name: "Classroom" });
    building.spaceInWalls(ctx, { level, inside: at(45, 15), number: "102", name: "Classroom" });

    // Size the main ducts first: 12 in deep to fit above the ceiling. Sizes come back in mm.
    const advice = ctx.read<{ suggested: { size: { width: number; height: number }; velocityFpm: number } }>("mechanical.duct_size", { cfm: SUPPLY_CFM, shape: "rect", height_mm: 305, system_kind: "supply_air" });
    const { width, height } = advice.suggested.size;
    const duct = routes.rect(units.mm(width), units.mm(height));

    // The unit's part type: a box with supply and return openings on its underside, sized like the ducts.
    // A route or layout script saves a new type as an edit (save_part_types). It never calls
    // ctx.parts.define (only a part script does); to use a type the model or library already has,
    // list its id in reads.partTypes and place it with equipment.place.
    const rtu = parts.part("Rooftop unit", { type: "10 ton", category: "mechanical_equipment" });
    rtu.box({ length: units.in(120), width: units.in(60), height: units.in(48) });
    for (const [id, label, systemKind, x] of [["supply", "Supply", "supply_air", -30], ["return", "Return", "return_air", 30]] as const) {
      rtu.connector("bottom", { id, label, domain: "duct", systemKind, shape: "rect", width: units.mm(width), height: units.mm(height), offset: [units.in(x), units.in(0)] });
    }
    ctx.edit({ type: "save_part_types", label: "Rooftop unit, 10 ton", types: [{ typeId: "example.rtu.10t", definition: rtu.build() }] });

    // On the roof: its base 14 ft above the floor, over the middle wall.
    const unit = equipment.place(ctx, { level, type: "example.rtu.10t", at: at(30, 15), height: ft(14), mark: "RTU-1" });

    // Supply down into room 101, return down into room 102, both at 11 ft (above the 10 ft ceiling).
    routes.along(ctx, { level, domain: "duct", size: duct, system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air", name: "Supply air" }, height: ft(11), from: unit.connector("supply"), points: [at(15, 15), at(8, 15)] });
    routes.along(ctx, { level, domain: "duct", size: duct, system: { id: "ra-1", kind: "return_air", name: "Return air" }, height: ft(11), from: unit.connector("return"), points: [at(45, 15), at(52, 15)] });

    // A mechanical plan cut above the ducts, every duct tagged with its size.
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level, name: "Level 1 - Mechanical", scale: 48, cutHeight: ft(12), discipline: "mechanical" });
    documents.autoTag(ctx, { view: plan, categories: ["duct", "equipment"] });

    // The plan and an equipment schedule on sheets.
    const planSheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-101", name: "Level 1 mechanical plan" });
    documents.place(ctx, planSheet, plan, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(280) });
    const schedule = documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Mechanical equipment schedule", category: "mechanical_equipment", columns: ["mark", "type_name", "level"] });
    const scheduleSheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-601", name: "Mechanical schedules" });
    documents.place(ctx, scheduleSheet, schedule, { x: units.mm(200), y: units.mm(400) });

    ctx.label(`RTU-1 (${SUPPLY_CFM} CFM) with ${Math.round(width / 25.4)}x${Math.round(height / 25.4)} supply and return ducts at ${Math.round(advice.suggested.velocityFpm)} fpm`);
  },
});
```

## Plumbing riser

Toilet rooms on two floors with their fixture units counted, branches, a stack and a building drain sized by the plumbing code and sloped 1/4 in per ft, the fixtures connected, water demand from the Hunter curve, and the drain tagged with size and slope.

Run it: `npm run example -- plumbing-riser`, or paste it to an assistant connected to the tool server. Source: [`packages/bim-script/examples/plumbing-riser.ts`](../../packages/bim-script/examples/plumbing-riser.ts).

```ts
/**
 * Plumbing riser: toilet rooms on two floors, drained by a stack into a
 * sloped building drain, every pipe sized by the plumbing code.
 *
 * The script counts drainage fixture units (DFU) and water supply fixture
 * units (WSFU) for the fixtures it places, sizes the floor branches, the
 * stack and the building drain with the code's drain sizing calc (2021
 * plumbing code tables), and the water demand with the Hunter curve. Then it
 * routes the piping with its fall, connects the fixtures, and tags the drain
 * and branches with their size and slope.
 *
 * Run it: paste it to an assistant connected to the MutinyBIM tool server
 * ("run this script"), or `npm run example -- plumbing-riser`.
 */
import { defineScript, units, routes, building, equipment, documents } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

const ft = units.ft;
const at = (x: number, y: number) => ({ x: ft(x), y: ft(y) });

/** Fixture units per fixture, public use (plumbing code drainage and supply fixture unit tables). */
const FIXTURES = [
  { type: "builtin:plumbing-wc-flush-tank@1", mark: "WC", x: 4, dfu: 4, wsfu: 5 },
  { type: "builtin:plumbing-wc-flush-tank@1", mark: "WC", x: 8, dfu: 4, wsfu: 5 },
  { type: "builtin:plumbing-lavatory@1", mark: "L", x: 12, dfu: 1, wsfu: 2 },
  { type: "builtin:plumbing-lavatory@1", mark: "L", x: 15, dfu: 1, wsfu: 2 },
];
/** 1/4 in per ft: the code minimum for drains 3 in and smaller, and the slope the sizing table is read at. */
const SLOPE = { rise: units.in(0.25), per: ft(1) };

export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    /** Size one drain by the code (3 in. at least where a water closet drains to it); the answer is nominal inches. */
    const drainSize = (role: "building_drain" | "horizontal_branch" | "stack", dfu: number): number => {
      const result = ctx.calc({ calc: "plumbing.size_drain", inputs: { role, dfu, slope_in_per_ft: 0.25, serves_water_closet: true }, plumbingEdition: "2021" });
      if (!result.ok) throw new Error(result.reason);
      return Number(result.run.values.find((v) => v.key === "size_nominal_in")?.value);
    };

    const floorDfu = FIXTURES.reduce((sum, f) => sum + f.dfu, 0);
    const floorWsfu = FIXTURES.reduce((sum, f) => sum + f.wsfu, 0);
    const floors = [building.level(ctx, { name: "Level 1", elevation: ft(0) }), building.level(ctx, { name: "Level 2", elevation: ft(12) })];
    const sanitary = { id: "san-1", kind: "sanitary", name: "Sanitary" } as const;
    const branchIn = drainSize("horizontal_branch", floorDfu);
    const stackIn = drainSize("stack", floorDfu);
    const drainIn = drainSize("building_drain", floorDfu * floors.length);

    const [ground, upper] = floors;
    if (!ground || !upper) throw new Error("Two floors expected.");
    const pipe = (inches: number) => routes.pipe(units.in(inches), "pvc");
    const lastPiece = (route: { segment(n: number): string }) => {
      // The kernel numbers a route's pieces s1, s2, … from its start.
      let n = 1;
      while (ctx.model.find(route.segment(n + 1))) n += 1;
      return route.segment(n);
    };

    // Fixtures in the same spot on each floor: two water closets and two lavatories along one wall.
    const fixturesOn = (level: string, floor: number) => FIXTURES.map((f) => equipment.place(ctx, { level, type: f.type, at: at(f.x, 4), mark: `${f.mark}-${floor}` }));

    // Level 2: a branch under the floor, falling west to the stack at x = 1 ft.
    const branch = routes.along(ctx, { level: upper, domain: "pipe", size: pipe(branchIn), system: sanitary, height: ft(-1), slope: SLOPE, flow: "with_points", points: [at(17, 2), at(2, 2)] });
    routes.connectInto(ctx, { from: fixturesOn(upper, 2).map((p) => ({ elementId: p.id, port: "w" })), into: branch.segment(1) });

    // The stack: drawn on Level 1, where it ends. It leaves the branch end straight (1 ft on), then drops
    // to 18 in under the Level 1 floor. The first point takes the branch end's height, after its fall.
    const stack = routes.along(ctx, { level: ground, domain: "pipe", size: pipe(stackIn), system: sanitary, from: routes.atRunEnd(branch.segment(1), "end"), points: [at(1, 2), { ...at(1, 2), height: ft(-1.5) }] });

    // The building drain: from the stack's foot (an elbow turns it), east 2.5 ft under the Level 1 floor to the street, falling 1/4 in per foot.
    const drain = routes.along(ctx, { level: ground, domain: "pipe", size: pipe(drainIn), system: sanitary, from: routes.atRunEnd(lastPiece(stack), "end"), height: ft(-2.5), slope: SLOPE, flow: "with_points", points: [at(2, 2), at(60, 2)] });

    // Level 1's fixtures drain straight into the building drain under them.
    routes.connectInto(ctx, { from: fixturesOn(ground, 1).map((p) => ({ elementId: p.id, port: "w" })), into: lastPiece(drain) });

    // Water demand for every fixture, from the Hunter curve.
    const demand = ctx.calc({ calc: "plumbing.hunter_demand", inputs: { wsfu: floorWsfu * floors.length, building_type: "office" } });
    const gpm = demand.ok ? Number(demand.run.values.find((v) => v.key === "design_gpm")?.value) : null;

    // A plumbing plan of Level 1, the building drain tagged with its size, slope and fixture units.
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: ground, name: "Level 1 - Plumbing", scale: 48, discipline: "plumbing" });
    documents.tag(ctx, { view: plan, element: lastPiece(drain), at: at(40, -3), fields: ["pipe.size", "pipe.slope", "pipe.carries.dfu"] });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "P-101", name: "Level 1 plumbing plan" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, plan, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(280) });

    ctx.label(`Riser: ${floorDfu * floors.length} DFU, ${branchIn} in branches, ${stackIn} in stack, ${drainIn} in building drain at 1/4 in per ft${gpm ? `, ${Math.round(gpm)} gpm water demand` : ""}`);
  },
});
```

## Electrical room

A one-bedroom unit: walls and rooms, a panel, receptacles placed by NEC 210.52 wall spacing, one circuit per room from a room template, and the panel schedule on a sheet with the code's demand factors.

Run it: `npm run example -- electrical-room`, or paste it to an assistant connected to the tool server. Source: [`packages/bim-script/examples/electrical-room.ts`](../../packages/bim-script/examples/electrical-room.ts).

```ts
/**
 * Electrical room: a one-bedroom unit's receptacles, circuits and panel
 * schedule.
 *
 * The script draws the unit's walls and rooms, places a panel, lets the
 * Electrical add-on propose receptacles by the code's wall spacing (NEC
 * 210.52: no point along a wall more than 6 ft from a receptacle), places
 * them, circuits them with a room template (one circuit per room), and puts
 * the panel's schedule on a sheet. The schedule prints the panel's loads
 * with the code's demand factors.
 *
 * Run it: paste it to an assistant connected to the MutinyBIM tool server
 * ("run this script"), or `npm run example -- electrical-room`.
 */
import { defineScript, units, building, equipment, documents } from "@permitzip/bim-script";

const ft = units.ft;
const at = (x: number, y: number) => ({ x: ft(x), y: ft(y) });
const box = (x0: number, x1: number) => [at(x0, 0), at(x1, 0), at(x1, 14), at(x0, 14)];
const NEC = "2023";

export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const level = building.level(ctx, { name: "Level 1", elevation: ft(0) });

    // A 32 ft x 14 ft unit: a bedroom and a living room, split by a wall at 14 ft.
    building.walls(ctx, { level, points: box(0, 32), closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level, points: [at(14, 0), at(14, 14)], thickness: units.in(4), height: ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level, number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: box(0, 14) });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level, number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: box(14, 32) });

    // The unit's panel, on the bedroom wall.
    const panel = equipment.place(ctx, { level, type: "builtin:panelboard-125-208-1ph@1", at: at(1, 13), mark: "LP-1" });

    // Receptacles by code spacing: the add-on proposes them, with the clause for each; the script keeps them all.
    const proposal = ctx.propose("electrical.receptacles", { typeId: "builtin:duplex-receptacle@1", roomIds: [bedroom, living], options: { mode: "dwelling", edition: NEC } });
    ctx.acceptGhosts(proposal.ghosts, proposal.summary);

    // One circuit per room, from a room template the script saves into the model.
    ctx.edit({ type: "save_catalog_entry", entry: { type: "circuit_template", name: "One-bedroom unit", description: "Each room's receptacles on their own circuit", rules: [{ room: "bedroom", devices: "receptacles" }, { room: "living", devices: "receptacles" }] } });
    const circuits = ctx.read<{ command: unknown; message: string }>("electrical.circuit_template_plan", { template: "One-bedroom unit", units: [{ panel: "LP-1", rooms: ["101", "102"] }] });
    ctx.editSteps(circuits.command);

    // The panel's loads with the code's demand factors, and its schedule on a sheet printed by the same rules.
    const loads = ctx.read<{ connectedVa: number; demand: { demandVa: number }; rules: { id: string } }>("electrical.loads", { panel: "LP-1", nec_edition: NEC });
    const schedule = documents.formSchedule(ctx, { kind: "panel", name: "Panel LP-1 schedule", element: panel.id, rules: loads.rules.id });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "E-601", name: "Panel schedules" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, schedule, { x: units.mm(250), y: units.mm(350) });

    // A power plan of the unit on its own sheet.
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level, name: "Level 1 - Power", scale: 48, discipline: "electrical" });
    const planSheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "E-101", name: "Level 1 power plan" });
    documents.place(ctx, planSheet, plan, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(280) });

    ctx.label(`${proposal.ghosts.length} receptacles (${proposal.passes ? "meets" : "short of"} NEC 210.52), ${circuits.message.toLowerCase()} LP-1 ${Math.round(loads.connectedVa)} VA connected`);
  },
});
```

# Edit commands (ctx.edit)

Every single edit a script may send with `ctx.edit`, read from the kernel's own schemas and those of the add-ons in force: 204 commands. The kit functions build these for you; reach for a command directly only when no kit function fits.

| [`add_field_block`](#add_field_block) | kernel |
| [`add_link_members`](#add_link_members) | kernel |
| [`add_local_rule`](#add_local_rule) | kernel |
| [`add_question`](#add_question) | kernel |

| [`auto_connect_runs`](#auto_connect_runs) | kernel |
| [`calibrate_underlay`](#calibrate_underlay) | kernel |
| [`change_elevation`](#change_elevation) | kernel |
| [`clear_classification`](#clear_classification) | kernel |

groups: {…}[]; grandTotals: boolean; itemize: boolean; presentation: {…} | {…}; display: {…}; pins?: {…}[] }; diagram?: { kind: string; hints?: {…} } }
- crop?: { min: { x: number; y: number }; max: { x: number; y: number } }
- keepViewportCenter?: boolean
